# PCA GA Minutes — LLM pack (compact catalogues, one file)

Generated index for AI ingestion. The corpus lives at https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga (raw markdown at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raymond-rishty/pca-ga/main).
This file concatenates the SMALL structured catalogues so you can load them in one fetch:
the corpus index, the RPR hub, judicial cases, constitutional inquiries, and CCB advice.
The provision-scoped BCO authority manifests are available at https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/api/bco/index.json; use them for provision-first retrieval.
Each catalogue row deep-links to the verbatim minutes page; cite as `M<GA>GA p.<page>`.
User-facing links in this pack are canonical GitHub Pages URLs ending in `.html`; source `.md` paths are for raw/repository retrieval only.

Use this pack only as a fallback for corpus-wide or cross-catalogue discovery when no narrower map applies; search it for candidate records, then open and cite the underlying pages.
Two catalogues are too large to inline here — fetch them directly when a question needs them:
- https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/OVERTURES.html — every overture + outcome (~104k tokens)
- https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/RPR-BY-PROVISION.html — RPR exceptions of substance by BCO/RAO/WCF provision (~308k tokens)



==============================================================================
# INDEX.md   (live: https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/INDEX.html)
==============================================================================

# PCA General Assembly Minutes — Corpus Index

This corpus contains all **52 volumes** of the Presbyterian Church in America *Minutes of the General Assembly*, **1973–2025**, as cleaned, OCR-corrected Markdown. It also includes structured catalogues. You can read the files here, search them with command-line tools, or use them in your own research tools.

## Catalogues

- **[Overtures](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/OVERTURES.html)** — every overture to every Assembly (number, source presbytery, page). *"Has the PCA considered this before?"*
- **[Judicial cases](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/CASES.html)** — SJC/CCB cases with parties, disposition, and the BCO / Westminster Standards provisions cited; the canonical metadata view is **[JUDICIAL-CASES.md](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/JUDICIAL-CASES.html)**; also **[by constitutional provision](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/CASES-BY-PROVISION.html)** with auditable tag sources and line evidence.
- **[Constitutional inquiries](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/INQUIRIES.html)** — questions of constitutional interpretation answered by the CCB, each with a Digest-level headnote and the verbatim record. *"What has the CCB said about this provision?"*
- **[CCB advice on overtures & amendments](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/CCB-OVERTURE-ADVICE.html)** — the CCB's constitutional review of proposed changes (whether an overture is *in conflict* with the Constitution).
- **[Review of Presbytery Records](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/RPR.html)** — exceptions of substance taken to each presbytery's minutes (the constitutional-compliance record), threaded across years with their satisfactory/unsatisfactory outcome; also **[by provision](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/RPR-BY-PROVISION.html)**. *"Which presbyteries were cited under this BCO provision, and was it resolved?"*
- **[Per-volume outlines](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/outlines/)** — a structural table of contents for each volume.
- **Full-text search:** a SQLite database (`pca_minutes.db`) indexes every page; see [../PORTABLE.md](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/PORTABLE.html) for query recipes. The markdown above is generated from it.

# RPR.md   (live: https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/RPR.html)

# Review of Presbytery Records (RPR) — Exceptions of Substance

Each year, the General Assembly's **Committee on Review of Presbytery Records** reviews presbytery minutes and records **exceptions of substance**, meaning apparent violations of the Constitution. This catalogue follows each exception from the original finding through the presbytery's response and a later Assembly's **satisfactory** or **unsatisfactory** disposition. It draws from the RPR appendix of every volume from GA18 through GA52 (1990–2025). The published appendix reflects the **adopted** report after floor deletions, and each affected row notes the relevant floor action.

## Corpus

- **5935 threaded exceptions of substance** across **100 presbyteries**, GA18–52 (1990–2025), from 10624 report appearances.
- Final disposition: **3333 satisfactory (closed)**, **884 unsatisfactory (outstanding)**, **1718 raised** (most-recent year, not yet adjudicated).
- Cross-reference by provision: **[RPR exceptions by BCO/RAO/WCF provision](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/RPR-BY-PROVISION.html)**.

## Citations to the Standing Judicial Commission (BCO 40-5)

Presbyteries cited to the SJC for repeated failure to submit minutes/responses or for serious non-compliance — the terminal escalation of the RPR process — with the related judicial case where one resulted.

# CASES.md   (live: https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/CASES.html)
==============================================================================

# Judicial Case Index

Cases decided by the Standing Judicial Commission (SJC) and its predecessor the Committee on Judicial Business (CJB), grouped by Assembly. For canonical case IDs, proceeding types, review standards, editorial summaries, BCO provisions, and topic tags, see **[JUDICIAL-CASES.md](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/JUDICIAL-CASES.html)**.

This index is **structure-first**: every case listed links to a full-text page re-extracted verbatim from the volume (with its opinions). After the decided cases, an Assembly may list extra rows from the underlying case table: *decided at Nth GA* — the case was only listed here (deferred to a later Assembly, or cited from an earlier one) and links to where it was actually decided; *reference / no separate decision* — a cross-reference, roll-up, or out-of-order/withdrawn matter with no published decision; *not yet re-extracted* — the volume is still pending.


## 3rd General Assembly (1975)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [3-12](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga03_1975__case1.html) | Rev. Harold L. Webb & Rev. Thomas Miller v. Pacific Presbytery | Dismissed | Ministers complained that Pacific Presbytery conducted nonroutine business without the constitutionally required quorum of three teaching and three ruling elders. The Assembly agreed that the August 4, 1975 actions were irregular, but dismissed the complaint because Presbytery later met with a quorum and ratified those actions. The dismissal therefore reflected correction of the defect, not approval of proceeding without a quorum. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga03_1975__case1.html) |

## 4th General Assembly (1976)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [4-12](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga04_1976__case1.html) | Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana v. Grace Presbytery | Remanded | Trinity Church complained that Grace Presbytery's July 9, 1976 substitute motion, delaying Adrian Pater's ordination until he was called to PCA work, was an out-of-order reconsideration. The Judicial Commission did not reach the merits: because the BCO 43-5 record was not complied with and minutes were inadequate, it returned the whole matter to the lower court for a new hearing. The Assembly accepted that judgment and separately adopted, 238–131, a recommendation that the BCO does not envisage ordination expressly for pastoral service in another denomination. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga04_1976__case1.html) |
| [4-13](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga04_1976__case2.html) | Session of Eastland Presbyterian Church, Memphis, Tennessee v. Covenant Presbytery | Not sustained | A session complained that Covenant Presbytery violated PCA standards by approving the summer employment of a divorced and remarried man in a ministerial capacity. The Judicial Commission found the complaint invalid, holding that McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity. It expressly did not decide whether such employment would violate the Constitution. The General Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment, leaving the presbytery's action undisturbed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga04_1976__case2.html) |

## 5th General Assembly (1977)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [5-13 / 5-87](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga05_1977__case1.html) | Rev. Paul L. Karlberg and Ruling Elder James G. Luce v. Central Georgia Presbytery | Not sustained | Complainants Karlberg and Luce challenged Central Georgia Presbytery’s commission as biased—it heard the Faith Church minority but not the majority—and challenged its judicial designation and recommendations. After Presbytery rescinded recommendations 2–6, complainants dropped those reasons, leaving only the bias claim. A General Assembly judicial commission heard both sides and unanimously declined to sustain. It reasoned both parties acted in good faith, mistakes were inadvertent, and remand would not further Christ’s cause. The rescinded recommendations and designation were not adjudicated. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga05_1977__case1.html) |
| [5-14 / 5-86](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga05_1977__case2.html) | Rev. [REDACTED] (Kim) v. Presbytery of Texas | Case deemed abandoned |  | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga05_1977__case2.html) |
| [5-15 / 5-83](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga05_1977__case3.html) | Rev. Thomas Barnes et al. v. Evangel Presbytery | Not sustained | The Fifth General Assembly approved its Judicial Commission’s refusal to sustain a complaint challenging Presbytery’s approval of Mercer for ordination as an evangelist without a call and for parachurch work outside its bounds. No reason for rejecting the complaint was stated. The ruling nevertheless required Presbytery to have—and itself issue—a written call before implementing the ordination decision, and requested referral of the broader question defining a valid ministerial call to the Permanent Committee on Judicial Business. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga05_1977__case3.html) |

## 6th General Assembly (1978)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [case](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga06_1978__case1.html) | James H. Campbell v. Mid-Atlantic Presbytery | Remanded | Ruling Elder James H. Campbell complained that Mid-Atlantic Presbytery approved a commission report finding charges against Rev. Robert Schoof inadmissible rather than proceeding on them. The General Assembly adopted the Committee on Judicial Business recommendation ordering Presbytery to hold a new hearing on the original charges under BCO 44-5, to conform to the BCO, and to keep the principals informed; it also appointed a judicial commission for any further complaint or appeal. The adopted report gives no further reasoning and does not expressly rule on the late-filing request. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga06_1978__case1.html) |
| [case](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga06_1978__case2.html) | Luther L. Allin Jr. et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery | Partially sustained; Denied; Remanded | Session members challenged Presbytery’s order to hold a congregational meeting on officer rotation and its handling of the complaint hearing. The Judicial Commission held that ten days ran from the notice’s postmark and that Bristow and Pastor Vitullo could not participate as members of the reviewing court. It nevertheless upheld Presbytery’s authority to require the meeting: a sufficient petition left the Session no option to refuse, while the congregation retained authority to decide rotation. The complaint was sustained in part and remanded for a properly noticed hearing. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga06_1978__case2.html) |

Presbytery of the Mid-Atlantic | Complaint partially sustained; Commission sustained complaint on grounds 1, 2, and 3; Presbytery directed to proceed with trial |  | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga07_1979__case1.html) |

## 8th General Assembly (1980)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [3](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga08_1980__case1.html) | Teaching Elders Byron Snapp and James M. Hope v. Calvary Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | Teaching Elders challenged Calvary Presbytery’s use of the extraordinary clause to examine and ordain a candidate who had completed only one quarter of Hebrew. The Assembly sustained the complaint’s single specification because Presbytery had not demonstrated either extraordinary circumstances or the man’s proven extraordinary gifts. It found the ordination contrary to the Book of Church Order and remanded for correction. Rather than answer the broader question about proper use of the clause, it ordered a report to the Ninth General Assembly. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga08_1980__case1.html) |
| [4](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga08_1980__case2.html) | Ruling Elder James H. Campbell et al. v. Presbytery of Mid-Atlantic | dismissed (absent complainant/counsel) |  | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga08_1980__case2.html) |
| [5](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga08_1980__case3.html) | Teaching Elder Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Remanded | Complainants challenged Presbytery's sustaining of ordination trials for a candidate who affirmed continuing revelation through interpreted tongues and its approval of a campus-ministry call lacking required terms. The Assembly sustained both counts, holding that the examination left the candidate's views unclarified and failed adequately to protect the Standards' teaching on the finality and sufficiency of Scripture; Presbytery conceded the call's omission. It remanded the matter to obtain a BCO 21-1-compliant call and re-examine the candidate. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga08_1980__case3.html) |

## 9th General Assembly (1981)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [case](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga09_1981__case1.html) | Ruling Elder Cooke Lewis, et al. v. Grace Presbytery | Not sustained | Members of a congregation challenged Grace Presbytery's formation of an administrative commission, its method of appointing the commission, and its refusal to dissolve the pastoral relationship after a 26-16 congregational vote. The General Assembly adopted its Judicial Commission's judgment declining to sustain each item or the complaint as a whole because none of the challenged actions violated the BCO. It also urged all parties to continue efforts toward reconciliation. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga09_1981__case1.html) |
| [case](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga09_1981__case2.html) | Ruling Elder Robert H. Zeigler v. Presbytery of Texas | Not sustained; Affirmed | A ruling elder complained that the Presbytery of Texas, handling a complaint against a session, appointed a committee rather than the requested commission and had that committee meet with the pastor, session members, and congregants before meeting the complainants. The Assembly adopted the Judicial Commission's report and unanimously confirmed the lower court's judgment (10-0). No adopted reasons or issue-level merits appear, so the case's value is a sparse example of a confirmed judgment without explanation. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga09_1981__case2.html) |
| [case](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga09_1981__case3.html) | Teaching Elder Rodney King, et al. v. Presbytery of Western Carolinas | Not sustained | A complaint challenged Presbytery's one-year delay before accepting a petition to organize a mission congregation. The General Assembly adopted the Judicial Commission's report and did not sustain the complaint. It reasoned BCO 5-1(1) gives Presbytery discretion over the time for organization, the group had sought only mission status, and the dispute was best handled at Presbytery, where complainants could seek reconsideration. A dissent recommending sustain and annulment was admitted but not adopted. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga09_1981__case3.html) |

## 10th General Assembly (1982)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case1.html) | Stephen M. Lee, et al. v. Gulf Coast Presbytery | Partially sustained | A Session challenged Gulf Coast Presbytery’s refusal to sustain Raymond Bradford Fell’s ordination examination, contending that his theonomic view was improperly treated as disqualifying and that prejudicial materials affected the process. The General Assembly sustained specifications 1, 2, and 5, but not 3 and 4. It ordered re-examination after direct guidance on specific biblical and confessional deficiencies, while expressly refusing to dictate the result. It also urged that no view of the judicial law’s present application should itself define orthodoxy or heresy. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case1.html) |
| [2](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case2.html) | Charles H. Davis, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia | Sustained | A teaching elder complained that Central Georgia Presbytery wrongly refused to sustain his complaint against a session that closed a disciplinary matter involving unbiblical separation, divorce, and remarriage before any judicial action. The General Assembly's Judicial Commission sustained the complaint, treating the session's "closing of the matter" as the central issue. It did not grant the requested reproof, suspension, or excommunication; it requested the presbytery to aid the session in corrections and heed WCF 24:6 and SC 87 on divorce and repentance. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case2.html) |
| [3](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case3.html) | David H. Bryson, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia | Sustained | Teaching elders challenged Central Georgia Presbytery’s refusal to sustain a complaint against Liberty Presbyterian Church’s Session for closing a disciplinary matter before taking judicial action. The General Assembly sustained the complaint, adopting findings that counseling, Session discussion, and instruction on discipline were underway before the Session closed the matter and refused to reopen it. It requested Presbytery to assist the Session with appropriate corrections or further action and said both courts should heed confessional teaching on marriage and repentance. The complainants’ requested affirmations were not expressly ordered. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case3.html) |
| [4](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case4.html) | Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr., et al. v. Grace Presbytery | Not sustained | Complainants challenged Grace Presbytery's refusal to ask the Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over allegations against a minister in Western Carolinas Presbytery. The Assembly did not sustain the complaint because Western Carolinas had not refused jurisdiction. It nevertheless directed that presbytery to proceed at its next stated meeting and held the one-year limitation inapplicable because its commission had unduly delayed formal process. The ruling was conditional, not an unqualified endorsement of the handling below. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case4.html) |
| [5](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case5.html) | James K. Workman, et al. (Session of Peace Presbyterian Church) v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Sustained | The Session challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to rescind its resolution calling voluntary total abstinence from alcohol the proper Christian lifestyle. The General Assembly unanimously sustained the complaint, adopting the commission’s conclusion that the resolution in practice bound consciences and exceeded Scripture’s requirements contrary to the Westminster Confession. The judgment did not expressly rescind the resolution, and it distinguished improper conscience-binding from permissible teaching and counseling against alcohol abuse and intemperance. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case5.html) |
| [6](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case6.html) | Session of First Presbyterian Church, Stanley, North Carolina v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Partially sustained | The Session challenged Presbytery’s refusal to receive complaints and associated voting, executive-session, elder-emeritus, interpretive, and disciplinary actions. The General Assembly sustained items 1, 2, and 5, but not 3, 4, and 6. Receiving a complaint under BCO 43-1 was not subject to a vote; when heard, complainants and respondents could not participate. Executive session was permissible, an elder emeritus retained full privileges, and item 6 was improper in this court. No reason was given for item 5. Presbytery was instructed to receive and hear the complaints properly. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case6.html) |

## 11th General Assembly (1983)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case1.html) | Robert L. Reymond et al. v. Illiana Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | A teaching elder confessed adultery, but Presbytery charged him only with ninth-commandment violations, admonished him, and required him to reconsider his call. The complaint alleged Presbytery failed to take BCO 34-7 action and improperly reduced the charges. The Commission sustained both items and remanded for a new trial, reasoning that the confessed sins were not considered and the censure was not commensurate with the offenses charged; it did not itself convict or sentence him. It adopted a recommendation directing Presbytery to follow BCO disciplinary procedures. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case1.html) |
| [13](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case10.html) | Donald A. Codling et al. v. Presbytery of Eastern Canada | Partially sustained | Presbytery members challenged Eastern Canada Presbytery’s denial of Ron Harris’s licensure. The complaint was sustained regarding the improperly adopted supermajority rule and the insufficiency of objections concerning counseling, evangelistic preaching, and sovereign grace; claims that pertinent data was excluded and requests to hear Harris preach were blocked were not sustained. Citing the fragmented examination and sharply differing views, the Assembly urged a complete reexamination at one meeting. It did not order Harris licensed or formally remand the matter. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case10.html) |
| [2](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case2.html) | Val H. Barleman et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension | Sustained; Annulled | The General Assembly sustained a complaint against Ascension Presbytery for sustaining a candidate's ordination trials despite exceptions to PCA constitutional standards. The Commission upheld specifications that his Lord's Supper and baptism views denied required visible-church membership and that his women-deacons view conflicted with the BCO; it rejected specifications on Sabbath recreation and immersion. The Assembly annulled the Presbytery's sustaining action, but not the ordination itself, so the candidate remained on the roll. It directed correction of the trial and pastoral instruction, with possible discipline if his views persisted. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case2.html) |
| [7](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case3.html) | Stark Wilbor et al. v. North Georgia Presbytery | Sustained; Annulled | Complainants challenged North Georgia Presbytery’s approval of John Parrish’s transfer examination after he denied that the first day of the week is the Christian Sabbath. The General Assembly sustained the specification of error and annulled Presbytery’s action, characterizing the teaching as a fundamental element of doctrine. Presbytery was directed to instruct Parrish and, only if his view conformed to Scripture, the doctrinal standards, and the BCO, re-examine him in that area. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case3.html) |
| [6](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case4.html) | "Determined Minority" of New Life Presbyterian Church v. Judicial Commission of Central Carolina Presbytery | Partially sustained | Members of New Life Presbyterian Church challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's commission over its handling of membership dismissals and compliance with earlier Assembly directions. The General Assembly commission held that the presbytery commission exceeded BCO 57-5 membership requirements and sustained a related item in part, but did not sustain the remaining claims, including that the commission had failed to act or caused the entire conflict. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case4.html) |
| [8](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case5.html) | Jack Eubanks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Partially sustained | Complainants challenged Presbytery’s called meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adopted adjudication sustained the objection to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote because Robert’s Rules required a two-thirds vote, and sustained without stated grounds the objection to ordering the dissolved commission to reassemble and revote. It rejected the challenges to the called meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its consideration of David Alexander’s complaint; the membership claim failed because church membership is not itself a court. No express remedy was ordered. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case5.html) |
| [10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case6.html) | David Lockwood Jr. and Evan Holyfield v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Partially sustained; Not sustained | David Lockwood Jr. and Evan Holyfield challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's commission for allegedly failing to act and mishandling discipline and reconciliation at New Life Presbyterian Church. The General Assembly commission rejected the failure-to-act claims, citing twenty-three meetings, and found that the complainants had not followed the reconciliation plan; it nevertheless sustained one overlapping membership-discipline item in part by reference to its ruling in Case 6. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case6.html) |
| [12](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case7.html) | Jack Eubanks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Partially sustained | Complainants challenged a called Presbytery meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adjudication sustained objections to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote and ordering the dissolved commission to reconvene and revote. A commission with power could be dismissed only by a two-thirds vote under Robert’s Rules; no separate ground was stated for the reconvening issue. Challenges to the meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its receipt of another complaint were not sustained. No relief was specified. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case7.html) |
| [15](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case8.html) | W. Ted Smith Jr. v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Not sustained | A presbytery was challenged for allegedly failing to carry out General Assembly directives restoring dismissed New Life congregation members and for allowing the pastor and session to evade compliance; the complainant asked the Committee on Judicial Business to dissolve the pastoral relation and impose censure. The CJB did not sustain the complaint. The supplied record states that disposition but contains no adopted reasoning, findings, or remedial order, so the basis for the ruling cannot be stated. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case8.html) |
| [9](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case9.html) | Session of Village Chapel Presbyterian Church v. Presbytery of Eastern Carolina | Abandoned; Affirmed | The Session of Village Chapel Presbyterian Church complained that Eastern Carolina Presbytery improperly lifted its matter from the table, alleging refusal of reasonable indulgence, improper evidence, and haste. The Commission adjudged the complaint abandoned: after public notice and a two-day recess, the complainant neither appeared nor sent counsel and gave no satisfactory explanation, as BCO 42-10 requires for complaints. Separately, it confirmed the SCJB's Reference 8 advice—six questions belonged in complaint or review and control; the seventh only required referring the applicant to the BCO. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case9.html) |
| [1983-12](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case7.html) | Jack Eubanks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Partially sustained | Complainants challenged a called Presbytery meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adjudication sustained objections to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote and ordering the dissolved commission to reconvene and revote. A commission with power could be dismissed only by a two-thirds vote under Robert’s Rules; no separate ground was stated for the reconvening issue. Challenges to the meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its receipt of another complaint were not sustained. No relief was specified. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case7.html) |
| [1983-14](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case14.html) | RE Truman Swain et al. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Abandoned | A session's complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery for lifting from the table a matter concerning the church was abandoned because neither the complainant nor counsel appeared before the Commission within two days, despite public notice and a recess, and no satisfactory explanation was given. The Commission also confirmed and adopted the SCJB's interim advice on Reference 8: six questions were properly declined as redressable by complaint or review and control, while the seventh only required referring the applicant to the BCO. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case14.html) |

## 12th General Assembly (1984)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [12-80](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case1.html) | Elder Roy J. Wuckovich v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Not sustained; Affirmed | A ruling elder complained that Central Carolina Presbytery violated the BCO in examining and approving Rick Downs for ordination, citing five specifications about the call, Downs’s Sabbath exception, the revote after an initial disapproval, lack of Scriptural search, and ordination questions. The judicial commission held points 1, 2, 4, and 5 not sustained 11–0 and point 3 not sustained 10–1; the general complaint was not sustained 11–0, and the lower court decision was confirmed. Its explanatory opinion said the commission disagreed on the Sabbath/subscription question and acted largely because the specifications did not substantiate the complaint. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case1.html) |
| [12-81](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case2.html) | Russell D. Toms and TE William L. Thompson v. Central Florida Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | Central Florida Presbytery received a minister while he had a pending call to labor in another presbytery. A Judicial Commission sustained the specification of error, holding that BCO 13-2,5 barred receiving him under those circumstances; the vote was 9–4. It also voted 13–0 to remand the entire matter for proper procedures regarding his admission to the PCA. The Commission commended the presbytery's aim of receiving him but ruled the process erroneous, leaving the admission to be handled through proper procedures. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case2.html) |
| [12-82](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case3.html) | Warren Gardner, et al. v. Presbytery of North Georgia | Not sustained | A complaint challenged North Georgia Presbytery's transfer of Trinity Mission, Elberton, Georgia, to Central Georgia Presbytery, alleging insufficient debate and failure to examine discipline issues. The Judicial Commission unanimously did not sustain the specification of error. Its adopted explanation found that two years of contact and discussions had done as much as possible to clear misunderstanding. It nevertheless noted the presbytery's inadequate explanation and the complainants' failure to secure adequate information; no relief was granted, and the listed questions about congregational choice and transfer power were not answered. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case3.html) |
| [12-83](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case4.html) | Session of Faith Presbyterian Church, Akron, Ohio, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension | Partially sustained | A Session and other complainants challenged Presbytery’s May 1984 resolution as continued noncompliance with directions from an earlier ordination case. The continued-noncompliance specification was sustained, but allegations of constitutional violation and contumacy were not sustained. Remedial recommendations were adopted, although the supplied excerpt provides neither their terms nor the deciding body’s reasons. The mixed ruling therefore distinguishes noncompliance from the complainants’ more serious characterizations of Presbytery’s conduct. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case4.html) |
| [12-83](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case5.html) | Carl W. Bogue, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension | Partially sustained | Ascension Presbytery was challenged for resolving not to comply with prior General Assembly directions concerning an ordination examination. The case was sustained as to continued noncompliance and constitutional violation, but not as to contumacy; remedial recommendations were adopted. The supplied text contains the complaint rather than the operative judgment, so it does not disclose the adjudicative reasoning or the specific remedial measures. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case5.html) |
| [12-83](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case6.html) | Robert C. Peterson, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension | Sustained | Complaint challenged Ascension Presbytery's March 10, 1984 refusal to obey the Eleventh General Assembly's directive to correct constitutional defects in Kurt Lutjens's ordination trial, and its purported BCO 41 reference of the matter to the Twelfth General Assembly for retrial. The CJB sustained specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation and adopted recommendations for remedial action. The complaint's asserted distinction—that BCO 41 cannot return a prior General Assembly decision for retrial—marks the case's practical limit. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case6.html) |

## 13th General Assembly (1985)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [5](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga13_1985__case1.html) | S. Michael Preg, Jr., et al. v. Missouri Presbytery | Sustained | Can a presbytery require an annual committee visit to every session and congregation absent a request or evident problem? The judicial commission sustained the complaint against Missouri Presbytery 16-0, holding BCO 11-4 limits higher-court jurisdiction to express constitutional provisions and BCO 13-9 contains no clear authorization for such required visits. It instructed presbytery to conform its Standing Rules and visitation procedures to the BCO, while encouraging voluntary pastoral oversight; several commissioners recorded negative votes without stated reasons. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga13_1985__case1.html) |
| [1985-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga13_1985__1985-04.html) | Mayfield v. Siouxlands Presbytery | Out of order (type not stated) | The Assembly found Jack Mayfield's appeal not in order under BCO 42-4 because he filed it nearly a year and a half after the matter had been adjudicated, and his reasons did not justify disregarding the filing requirement. The ruling did not reach the underlying merits and directed him instead to BCO 37-4's procedure for removing censure. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga13_1985__1985-04.html) |

## 14th General Assembly (1986)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case1.html) | Kenneth L. Gentry, Jr. et al. v. Calvary Presbytery | Sustained; Annulled; Remanded | Ministers challenged Calvary Presbytery's approval of William Hyer's examination and reception despite his belief that noncanonical, nonbinding revelation could continue. The Assembly sustained the complaint because PCA standards foreclose continuing revelation beyond illumination and providence. It annulled only the examination portion concerning revelation, suspending his reception, and instructed Presbytery to counsel and re-examine him, then report to the next Assembly. The majority deemed the record sufficient despite a dissent emphasizing Hyer's affirmation of Scripture's finality and the absence of an examination transcript. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case1.html) |
| [2](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case2.html) | Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr. et al. v. Grace Presbytery | Not sustained | A complaint challenged Grace Presbytery's approval and installation of a candidate who had been divorced for his own infidelity and had remarried; the complainants argued Scripture, the Westminster Confession, BCO 16-3, and the Seventh General Assembly's divorce report barred ordination. The Judicial Commission did not sustain any of the four specifications and upheld Presbytery's action. Its adopted reason was that the PCA's constitutional statements do not explicitly address divorce and remarriage for church officers; noting wide interpretive disagreement, it called for study. The ordination and installation remained undisturbed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case2.html) |
| [3](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case3.html) | Henry D. Knight, Jr. v. Palmetto Presbytery | Partially sustained; Remanded | A ruling elder challenged Palmetto Presbytery’s publication, as an appendix to meeting minutes, of a letter never discussed at that meeting, and its handling of his complaint. The Judicial Commission sustained specifications 1 and 3: Presbytery had not clearly declared the publication erroneous, and it risked harming Covenant’s Session. Specifications 2 and 4 failed because Presbytery timely referred the complaint, though its record was inaccurate, and acted in good faith. Despite Presbytery’s later deletion of the letter, the Commission remanded for a new hearing on specifications 1 and 3. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case3.html) |
| [4](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case4.html) | Edward A. Steele III v. Great Lakes Presbytery | Abandoned | An appeal challenged Great Lakes Presbytery's decision to divest TE Edward A. Steele III without censure and without judicial process, which he alleged followed an accusation that he was not engaged in his official duties. Steele alleged constitutional and discriminatory error and sought investigation, rescission, or erasure of his name. Because no one appeared to represent the appeal, the Committee on Judicial Business judged it abandoned, leaving the merits and requested relief undecided. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case4.html) |
| [5](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case5.html) | D. Keith Abee et al. v. James River Presbytery | Sustained; Reversed; Remanded | Five appellants challenged censures imposed after a Presbytery commission treated a Session's request for assistance as authority to initiate judicial process. The Assembly sustained all six specifications, holding that the commission lacked authority to proceed before charges were approved and that original jurisdiction remained with the Session. It reversed the censures, ordered their public removal, and remanded for the Session to address any properly specified charges. The ruling expressly did not determine the appellants' guilt or innocence. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case5.html) |
| [6](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case6.html) | Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension | Sustained | Presbytery’s response claiming that Lutjens had changed his sacramental views was challenged as factually false and as a retroactive rewriting of minutes Presbytery had previously refused to interpret. All five specifications were sustained, including illegitimate interpretation of BCO 58-4. Because the earlier examination transcript was unavailable through mechanical failure, Presbytery was ordered to reexamine Lutjens, provide a complete transcript, and report by November 10, 1986. Discipline remained conditional on continued nonconformity after pastoral counsel. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case6.html) |
| [8](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case7.html) | Dye et al. v. Missouri Presbytery | Sustained; Annulled; Remanded |  | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case7.html) |

Great Lakes Presbytery | Out of order (type not stated) | The Committee on Judicial Business found Case 7, the six complaints of RE Dye et al. against the Presbytery of Missouri, to be in order and recommended that a single commission be appointed to adjudicate all six complaints. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case7_shell.html) |

## 15th General Assembly (1987)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [15-73](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga15_1987__case1.html) | Erwin Morrison, TE Donald Stone, TE David Brewer, TE Steve Christian, RE John Harley, RE David Lachman, RE George Harris v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Sustained | Philadelphia Presbytery ordained Lester Porter as a Ruling Elder of Presbytery to serve a cross-cultural mission church with no particular-church members. The Assembly, adopting the Judicial Commission's adjudication, sustained all three specifications and upheld the complaint: the ordination lacked BCO compliance and the Presbytery mishandled the complaint. It refused to annul Porter's ordination—reasoning Presbytery may ordain Ruling Elders in organizing churches—but directed Presbytery to find a BCO-conforming temporary government for Church Without Walls, stop ordaining Ruling Elders not duly elected by a particular church, and bring Porter's ordination into conformity. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga15_1987__case1.html) |

## 16th General Assembly (1988)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case1.html) | Carl Fox v. Mississippi Valley Presbytery et al | Partially sustained; Remanded | Fox challenged a Session’s acceptance of his resignation while censured, refusal to restore him, denial of relevant records, and allegedly uneven discipline in his marital dispute. The Assembly adopted the commission’s judgment sustaining the first, third, and fourth complaints: he remained a member, so his removal and nonrestoration were improper and he was entitled to relevant records. Those matters were remanded for rectification. The uneven-discipline claim was neither sustained nor denied because the evidence was insufficient; it too was remanded for investigation and necessary action. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case1.html) |
| [3](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case2.html) | David C. Lachman et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Sustained; Annulled | Complainant elders challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's tie-vote refusal to sustain its judicial commission's judgment that the Calvary Session wrongly treated physical cruelty as biblical grounds for divorce. The General Assembly adopted the commission's judgment sustaining all three specifications: the Session's action contravened Matthew 5 and 19, WCF 24:6, and the church's disciplinary role. It annulled Presbytery's refusal and instructed Presbytery to advise the Session that physical cruelty is not biblical or confessional grounds for divorce. The explanatory opinion urged pastoral alternatives, such as separation and rehabilitation, before any divorce determination. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case2.html) |
| [5](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case3.html) | Robert G. Rayburn et al. v. Missouri Presbytery | Not sustained; Affirmed | Missouri Presbytery instructed its Candidates and Credentials Committee to examine candidates without treating a qualified minority view on prophecy and tongues as disqualifying. Complainants argued this conflicted with the 1986 Gentry decision. The Judicial Commission, adopted by the 16th General Assembly, did not sustain the complaint and confirmed the lower court 7-4. Although earlier similar cases had annulled lower-court actions, it cited the absence of a specific candidate, safeguards, inconclusive debate, and a preference for grass-roots resolution, encouraging Overture 25. The dissent called the view fundamentally out of accord. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case3.html) |
| [7](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case4.html) | Robert Jamison v. Western Carolina Presbytery | Not sustained; Affirmed | A ruling elder complained that Western Carolina Presbytery wrongly left a confessing bisexual Teaching Elder under indefinite suspension rather than deposing him, excluding him from the sacraments, and cutting him off from fellowship. The General Assembly's adjudicating commission did not sustain the specification of error and confirmed Presbytery's action, holding it complied with BCO 30-3, 4 and 34-7. Review was limited to the constitutionality of the disciplinary process; the commission cited Presbytery's restorative purpose and evidence of repentance. The Assembly was advised Presbytery later deposed the Teaching Elder. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case4.html) |
| [8](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case5.html) | John Neville v. Western Carolina Presbytery | Withdrawn | The complaint was withdrawn after the matter was resolved at a called meeting of Western Carolina Presbytery on June 6, 1988. The published adjudication records no decision on the complaint's merits. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case5.html) |
| [10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case6.html) | James Serio et al. v. Palmetto Presbytery | Sustained | The 16th General Assembly approved the adjudicating Commission’s judgment sustaining a complaint against Palmetto Presbytery. The Commission found that Presbytery erred by sustaining John Tomlinson’s theology examination and licensing him despite his belief in continuing noncanonical revelation through prophecy, tongues, dreams, visions, and direct speech, contrary to WCF I.1 and I.6 and BCO 7-1. It directed Presbytery to annul the theology examination, suspend its licensing action, counsel and re-examine Tomlinson, exercise greater care, and report to the next Assembly. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case6.html) |
| [1988-11](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case11.html) | Korean Church of Washington Matter | In order | Korean Church of Washington complaint. Cross-referenced to 16-12, p. 114 and 16-57, p. 133, and Appendix V, p. 539, with no further detail recorded here. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case11.html) |

## 17th General Assembly (1989)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1 (from 16th GA)](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case1.html) | McCready et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Denied; Affirmed | Complaint by Douglas McCready et al. against Philadelphia Presbytery was found in order and referred to a commission for adjudication. No full case record or opinion appears in this window. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case1.html) |
| [4 (from 16th GA)](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case2.html) | TE Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Partially sustained; Annulled | Philadelphia Presbytery ordered Christ Church, Oreland’s Session to transfer three ruling elders while their judicial cases were on appeal. The General Assembly adopted its special Judicial Commission’s judgment rejecting the improper-debate specification for insufficient documentation but sustaining the constitutional challenge: BCO 12-5 and the separation of church-court powers reserve membership control to the Session, which correctly withheld transfer during pending judicial process. The judgment annulled Presbytery’s instruction and imposed three-year constitutional-inquiry safeguards, plus Digest purchase and officer review. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case2.html) |
| [6 (from 16th GA)](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case3.html) | TE John T. DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Sustained; Annulled; Guilty; Not guilty | A complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s approval of proceedings that cleared teaching and ruling elders without properly trying serious public accusations arising from Christ Church’s division. All three specifications were sustained because plea bargaining, dropped charges, and failure to hear necessary witnesses left the accusations unresolved. Presbytery’s action was annulled and de novo trials produced mixed convictions and acquittals. Harold Burkhart received six months’ suspension, Douglas McCready an admonition, and six former ruling elders three-month suspensions. The decision stressed taking such conflicts to Presbytery or judicial process rather than the congregation. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case3.html) |
| [9 (from 16th GA)](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case4.html) | Morrison et al. v. Those and a constitutional-limits specification were sustained; claims that Presbytery neglected underlying questions and acted for the Session were not. The March 12 actions were annulled, specified language expunged, and Presbytery directed to adopt safeguards for constitutional inquiries and review relevant church-law materials. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case4.html) |
