## 18th General Assembly (1990)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga18_1990__case1.html) | First Presbyterian Church of Rowlett, Texas v. North Texas Presbytery | Not sustained; Denied; Affirmed | A church challenged North Texas Presbytery’s approval of Rev. C. Don Darling, who disclosed that he could not conscientiously accept or conduct remarriage after divorce. The Standing Judicial Commission did not sustain and denied the complaint, affirming Presbytery. Ministerial acceptance ordinarily rests within a presbytery’s jurisdiction, and Darling’s exception neither concerned a fundamental of the doctrinal system nor struck at the vitals of religion or threatened much injury. Overriding Presbytery would therefore improperly impair liberty of conscience. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga18_1990__case1.html) |
| [2](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga18_1990__case2.html) | First Presbyterian Church of Rowlett, Texas v. North Texas Presbytery | Abandoned; Affirmed | First Presbyterian Church of Rowlett appealed after North Texas Presbytery reversed the Session's indefinite suspension of two members who had begun attending other churches. The SJC did not reach the asserted procedural errors because the Session advised that it would start over and would not pursue the appeal. Under BCO 43-7, the appeal was abandoned and Presbytery's judgment was affirmed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga18_1990__case2.html) |
| [1990-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga18_1990__case1.html) | First Presbyterian Church of Rowlett, Texas v. North Texas Presbytery | Not sustained; Denied; Affirmed | A church challenged North Texas Presbytery’s approval of Rev. C. Don Darling, who disclosed that he could not conscientiously accept or conduct remarriage after divorce. The Standing Judicial Commission did not sustain and denied the complaint, affirming Presbytery. Ministerial acceptance ordinarily rests within a presbytery’s jurisdiction, and Darling’s exception neither concerned a fundamental of the doctrinal system nor struck at the vitals of religion or threatened much injury. Overriding Presbytery would therefore improperly impair liberty of conscience. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga18_1990__case1.html) |
| [1990-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga18_1990__case2.html) | First Presbyterian Church of Rowlett, Texas v. North Texas Presbytery | Abandoned; Affirmed | First Presbyterian Church of Rowlett appealed after North Texas Presbytery reversed the Session's indefinite suspension of two members who had begun attending other churches. The SJC did not reach the asserted procedural errors because the Session advised that it would start over and would not pursue the appeal. Under BCO 43-7, the appeal was abandoned and Presbytery's judgment was affirmed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga18_1990__case2.html) |

## 19th General Assembly (1991)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1990-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-03.html) | Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church v. New River Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained | Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church complained against New River Presbytery's action sustaining a complaint that a Sunday school teacher holding theistic evolution and other doctrinal exceptions should not teach. The SJC partially sustained the complaint, declining to refer the matter back to the church with instructions but advising that the teacher should not teach while he holds exceptions that could require him to teach contrary to the fundamentals of the system of doctrine. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-03.html) |
| [1990-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-04.html) | Chappell v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Sustained | Ruling Elder Chappell complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's Commission, which had suspended the session of Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church and constituted itself as a 'Session Pro Tem' without due process or congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO grants no authority for a presbytery to depose a session and act in its place, that suspension requires due process, and that the congregation has an inalienable right to be governed by officers it has chosen. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-04.html) |
| [1990-04a](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-04a.html) | Marshall v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Sustained | Teaching Elder Wallace Marshall complained against the same Eastern Carolina Presbytery actions at Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church that were the subject of Case 90-4, filed separately as a Teaching Elder complainant. The SJC sustained this complaint on essentially the same grounds as Case 90-4, finding that the presbytery lacked authority to suspend the session without due process and to constitute itself as a 'Session Pro Tem.' | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-04a.html) |
| [1990-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-05.html) | Melton et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery | Denied | Complainants challenged the ruling of the session of Westminster Presbyterian Church (Chattanooga) disallowing proxy votes at a December 10, 1989 congregational meeting that voted not to rescind the earlier dissolution and property transfer to New City Fellowship. The SJC denied all specifications, holding that proxy voting was not required under BCO 24-4 or Robert's Rules, and that the congregation's decision to dissolve was within its rights under BCO Chapter 25. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-05.html) |
| [1990-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-07.html) | Stringer v. Mississippi Valley Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Remanded | Randy Stringer appealed his excommunication by Mississippi Valley Presbytery after being deposed and then excommunicated for failure to respond to the presbytery. The SJC set aside the excommunication and remanded the case to MVP, holding that after deposition the presbytery was required under BCO 46-8 to assign Stringer to membership in a particular church rather than proceed to excommunication. Dr. Morton H. Smith dissented, arguing that the presbytery had proper grounds to proceed to excommunication after Stringer's contumacy. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-07.html) |
| [1990-08](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-08.html) | Bowen v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Sustained | Bowen challenged Presbytery’s attempt, two years after installation, to rescind its earlier ruling and annul local officers’ elections and ordinations without trial. The SJC sustained the complaint: ordination is perpetual, deposition requires judicial process, and rescission was out of order after implementation; Presbytery likewise could not suspend a local elder without due process. But it affirmed that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals admitting no officer exception. The officers remained in office but doctrinally out of accord; voluntary demission or proper process was advised. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-08.html) |
| [1990-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-09.html) | Hathaway v. Grace Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | TE Vaughn Hathaway complained that the Session of Waynesboro Presbyterian Church failed to institute discipline against seven members who had not attended worship for over a year. The judicial panel denied the complaint on the grounds that the Session retained discretion to determine the timing of discipline proceedings, and procedural errors did not result in material prejudice. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-09.html) |
| [1990-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-10.html) | Hathaway v. Grace Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained; Moot | A pastor complained that Presbytery upheld his Session’s refusal to give him financial reports prepared for Session members, while also alleging record-transmission, circularization, factual, and constitutional errors. The SJC denied Specifications 1–5 but sustained Specification 6: because the pastor was a Session member, the Session’s authorization made the reports available to him regardless of whether other elders collected copies. His pastoral relationship had ended, however, so the access claim was moot and conferred no present right to the reports. Reasons for Specifications 1–2 were adopted from Case 90-9. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-10.html) |
| 1983-11 | Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery | withdrawn |  | _reference (decided earlier)_ · [ga19_1991 p.62](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/markdown/ga19_1991.html#ga19-p62) |

## 20th General Assembly (1992)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1991-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-01.html) | Sandra Lovelace v. Northeast Presbytery | Administratively out of order; Judicially out of order | The SJC found two attempted complaints administratively and judicially out of order. The October 1990 filing did not satisfy BCO 43-2 because the earlier letters it invoked had merely asked questions or communicated concern, rather than first presenting a complaint to Presbytery, and concerned an oral report not made part of Presbytery's record. The January 1991 filing supplied no supporting reasons as BCO 43-3 required and challenged specifications of error that were not themselves acts or decisions of Presbytery. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-01.html) |
| [1991-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-02.html) | Nickoley and Stephens v. Southwest Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained | Complainants challenged Southwest Presbytery's January 1991 actions: withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving Pastor Pollock's pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of Covenant PC's session. The SJC did not sustain the complaint and affirmed. It held the BCO gives no presbytery authority to suspend a session or act as a Session pro tem without formal congregational consent; BCO 31-1 left the elder charges with the session, so they were never validly before Presbytery; the dissolution challenge was moot after Pollock left the PCA, though Presbytery acted correctly on the congregation's request. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-02.html) |
| [1991-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-03.html) | Daniel R. Morse v. Covenant Presbytery | Abandoned; Moot | On Covenant Presbytery’s mixed BCO 41 reference, the SJC held that ministers Morse and Crenshaw could not resign unilaterally; joining another evangelical church invoked BCO 38-3, requiring their names erased, with notice that they were in good standing and faced no pending charges. Grace Church’s withdrawal required a congregational vote, not notice to Presbytery, so its name also was to be erased. Grace had abandoned its complaints, rendering them moot; the SJC nevertheless opined that recording a protest is insulated from complaint by BCO 45-5. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-03.html) |
| [1991-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-04.html) | Robert D. Hopper v. James River Presbytery | Denied | The SJC denied Hopper's complaint against James River Presbytery's April 13, 1991 order barring him from teaching or preaching his views on prophecy and tongues. It rejected all five specifications: Scripture did not forbid the order; the 1974 Pastoral Letter did not address presbytery's power to enjoin such teaching; forbearance did not preclude protecting peace and purity; presbytery could restrict preaching short of a heresy finding without binding conscience; and allowing presbyteral discussion while restricting congregational teaching was not inconsistent. The action remained in force. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-04.html) |
| [1991-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-05.html) | Herman Gunter III et al. v. Central Florida Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | Two ruling-elder nominees challenged the Session’s refusal to approve them based on their theonomic views and perceived divisiveness. The full SJC denied the complaint, holding that the court of original jurisdiction may assess an unsettled theological position and whether it threatens the church’s peace, purity, or progress; divisiveness was therefore properly considered. The ruling did not decide the merits of theonomy itself, and it left undisturbed Presbytery’s annulment of the Session’s categorical statement that theonomy violated WCF 19.4. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-05.html) |
| [1991-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-07.html) | Complainants v. Potomac Presbytery | Not sustained; Dismissed | Complainants challenged Potomac Presbytery's 11/12/91 adjudication denying their complaint over the Timonium Presbyterian Church pastoral dispute, arguing they received too little time, deliberation, and explanation. The SJC held the complaint not sustained: a higher court may not overturn a competent lower court merely because complainants are dissatisfied with the amount of input or time spent, and no constitutional defect was demonstrated. Two earlier complaints were dismissed as not timely filed. The timely 12/11/91 complaint was heard 3/6/92. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1991-07.html) |
| [1992-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1992-03.html) | Richard E. Olson, et al. v. Heritage Presbytery | Administratively out of order | Heritage Presbytery adopted a committee report answering a session's reference on whether a session may require officers to abstain from beverage alcohol. Olson and others complained. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order because it was not timely filed with the General Assembly, and independently ruled that a court's response to a non-judicial reference seeking advice under BCO 41-3 is not complainable. Complainants may submit their questions to the Committee on Constitutional Business. Confirmed 23-0. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1992-03.html) |
| [1992-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1992-04.html) | William A. Conrad, et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Administratively out of order; Remanded | Complainants alleged Central Carolina Presbytery failed to act when it remanded their complaints against the Prosperity Presbyterian Church Session to the commission acting as Interim Session. The SJC held Presbytery did not fail to act: that Interim Session was the court of original jurisdiction and should adjudicate the complaints timely. The SJC judged the complaint administratively out of order and remanded it to the Interim Session, reminding complainants of their right to appeal to a higher court. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga20_1992__1992-04.html) |
| 1992-06 | Conrad et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery. (Case #1) | administrative | Central Carolina Presbytery remanded complaints to an Interim Session Commission rather than adjudicating them directly. The SJC confirmed this action, finding that the Commission appointed as Interim Session was the proper court of original jurisdiction and remanding the complaints for adjudication by that Commission. | _decided at 21st GA_ · [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-06.html) |

## 21st General Assembly (1993)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1991-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1991-06.html) | Lovelace v. Northeast Presbytery (Case #2)  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained | A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal, after investigation, to try four elders on favoritism charges and its ruling that her related complaint was out of order because dissolution of her church ended her PCA membership. The SJC denied the first item because BCO 31-2 permits declining process when investigation raises no strong presumption of guilt. It sustained the second: jurisdiction properly invoked while a communicant member is not lost through a later status change. No remand was expressly ordered. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1991-06.html) |
| [1992-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-01.html) | Smith v. Northeast Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | Smith challenged Northeast Presbytery’s ruling that his complaint was untimely and unconstitutional after it dissolved Grace Church and indefinitely postponed a proposed Braintree mission. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded it for Presbytery adjudication. The May action first revealed Presbytery’s view that former members were outside the PCA, so the June complaint was timely. BCO 11-4 neither barred nor itself required care; responsibility arose here from the April referral to Presbytery’s missions committee. Care need not take the form of a mission, and mere dissolution alone would not create that responsibility. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-01.html) |
| [1992-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-02.html) | Roberts v. New River Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained | A congregation member complained that New River Presbytery erred in November 1991 by declining to accept TE Don Post Jr.'s resignation and dissolve his pastoral relation, instead appointing a commission. The SJC sustained the complaint. Under BCO 23-1, once the congregation concurred and no sufficient reasons to retain the pastor appeared, the resignation 'shall be accepted' and the relation dissolved; the Presbytery's general BCO 13-9 power did not override that specific provision. The Presbytery had already dissolved the relation on December 7, 1991; the adopted judgment ordered no remand. Three commissioners dissented. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-02.html) |
| [1992-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-05.html) | Parks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | Complainants challenged a Session plan under which most elders voluntarily resigned, the Session granted severance and benefits to its former pastor, proposed about a year with an interim pastor before a permanent call, and contemplated revising local bylaws. The SJC denied all four items. It held that the BCO permitted jointly considered voluntary resignations, that severance concerned resignation and the budget rather than a pastoral call, and that the plan and bylaw proposal were not themselves unconstitutional. Any later call still had to follow the BCO without undue delay, and local bylaws had to remain consistent with it. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-05.html) |
| [1992-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-06.html) | Conrad et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery. (Case #1)  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained; Denied | After a congregation voted to ask that all ruling elders' official relationships be dissolved without censure, the Session concurred and requested an interim Session. The SJC denied the elders' complaint, holding that BCO 24-6b extends by good and necessary deduction from one elder to multiple identified elders. Dissolution ended their service on that Session but did not divest them of office. Because both the congregation and Session requested it, BCO 13-9 and 15-2 authorized Presbytery to appoint an interim Session. A separate constitutional inquiry was denied without explanation. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-06.html) |
| [1992-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-07.html) | Conrad et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery (Case #2)  ·  *dissent* | Denied | A complaint arising from Central Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to prosecute TE Stephen O. Stout and to recognize his accusers as voluntary prosecutors was denied. The SJC framed two issues and answered both yes: the Presbytery could constitutionally adopt its Investigative Committee report and decline judicial process, because the Committee found no “strong presumption of guilt” under BCO 31-2; and it could refuse voluntary-prosecutor status, because BCO 31-1/31-3 left discipline to the Presbytery and made any voluntary prosecutor subject to its approval. The complaint was denied on both issues. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-07.html) |
| [1992-08](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-08.html) | Reference from Central Carolina Presbytery | Denied; Referred | Central Carolina Presbytery asked the SJC to adjudicate two complaints and a related reference concerning charges against church members. Although initially found administratively in order, the reference was declined because adjudicating only the formally referred matters could render at least two additional, related complaints moot without due consideration. All matters in Case 92-8 were returned to Presbytery; no underlying merits were decided. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-08.html) |
| [1992-09b](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-09b.html) | Overman v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Out of order (type not stated); Dismissed | Overman carried to the General Assembly his complaint that Eastern Carolina Presbytery improperly licensed Arthur Peterson, after the presbytery denied it. The SJC found the complaint not in order for lack of standing: Overman was not subject to the presbytery's jurisdiction (BCO 43-1; MSJC 6.2). It made no merits ruling; the same basic issue was noted as pending in a complaint by the Antioch Presbyterian Church session. The source header labels the disposition 'dismissed.' | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-09b.html) |
| [1992-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-10.html) | Mr. and Mrs. Matthew Bernard v. Ascension Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Administratively out of order | The Bernards appealed directly to the General Assembly from their excommunication by a Presbytery commission acting as the congregation’s Session. The SJC ruled the appeal administratively out of order because an appeal must first go to the next higher court—Ascension Presbytery—not to the court of original jurisdiction. It did not decide whether the excommunication was proper; that issue remained for Presbytery to hear. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga21_1993__1992-10.html) |
| 2013-09 | Marshall v. Pacific | dismissed |  | _decided at 42nd GA_ · [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga42_2014__stub_2013-09.html) |

## 22nd General Assembly (1994)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1992-09a](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1992-09a.html) | Antioch Session v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained | Antioch Session challenged Peterson’s licensure based on his prior divorce, creation and local-flood views, reversal of a committee recommendation, and close vote; it also challenged his regular preaching before licensure. The SJC rejected the licensure specifications because Presbytery had thoroughly examined repentance and doctrinal adherence, and no definitive PCA standard required exclusion on these facts. It sustained the pre-licensure supply issue under BCO 19-1, 22-5, and 22-6 and enjoined greater future circumspection. The licensure remained undisturbed; the ruling was expressly case-specific. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1992-09a.html) |
| [1993-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1993-01.html) | Smith v. Northeast Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | Smith complained that Northeast Presbytery failed to provide pastoral care after dissolving Grace Presbyterian Church. The SJC rejected Presbytery's objections that the complaint lacked supporting reasons or was barred by Smith's protest, held it in order, but denied it on the merits. Distinguishing the pastoral 'power of order' from judicial 'power of jurisdiction,' the SJC ruled that the Constitution neither requires nor permits a presbytery to retain jurisdiction over individual members of a dissolved particular church, and that pastoral care of former members is generally discretionary; on these facts, Presbytery's efforts satisfied any duty. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1993-01.html) |
| [1993-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1993-02.html) | Johnson v. Evangel Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained | An appeal challenged Evangel Presbytery's judgment that a teaching elder wrongfully pursued divorce without biblical grounds, alleging procedural irregularities, refused evidence, haste, prejudice, and mistaken censure. The SJC rejected each claim: failure to swear two minor witnesses was acknowledged and nonprejudicial, notices and defense opportunity were adequate, and the guilty finding rested on Scripture, WCF 24:6, BCO 26-1, and 30-3; the 1992 study did not authorize divorce for alleged spiritual desertion. The appeal was not sustained, leaving the indefinite suspension in force; one commissioner dissented. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1993-02.html) |
| [1993-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1993-03.html) | Chen v. Ascension Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Reversed; Other |  | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1993-03.html) |

| [1993-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1993-05.html) | Clark v. Southwest Presbytery (Request for Clarification)  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Remanded | John P. Clark, Jr. requested clarification of the SJC decision in Case 93-5 regarding who controls the assets of South Valley Presbyterian Church, Inc. after the congregation voted to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC held it lacked jurisdiction over the civil corporate entity and its property, declining to rule on Clark's request. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga22_1994__1993-05.html) |

Tennessee Valley Presbytery (Appeal) | Remanded | After Tennessee Valley Presbytery deposed a minister without conducting a church trial, he appealed, alleging denial of PCA due process. The SJC remanded for a new trial. It held that Presbytery could bring charges but could not substitute the Papua New Guinea criminal proceedings for ecclesiastical process, especially when it neither served an indictment and charges nor appointed counsel for an accused unable to attend. The remand permitted a constitutionally compliant trial; it did not resolve guilt or bar discipline. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga25_1997__1995-10.html) |

Mississippi Valley Presbytery | Sustained | Complainants challenged Mississippi Valley Presbytery’s approval of James Blaha’s ordination examination, arguing that his views on tongues and prophecy were constitutional exceptions and precluded approval. The SJC agreed that Presbytery should have acknowledged and noted the exceptions, but upheld the examination. It found no proof that Blaha’s denial that the gifts conveyed revelation crossed prior Assembly limits and deferred to Presbytery on an unsettled issue. It expressly declined reexamination or remand; a substantial partial dissent would have set the examination aside. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga25_1997__1995-11.html) |

## 26th General Assembly (1998)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1997-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__stub_1997-01.html) | Felton v. Grace Presbytery | Withdrawn | A complaint docketed as Case 97-1, Felton v. Grace Presbytery, was withdrawn by the complainant in the 26th Assembly records. No merits opinion was published, and the available notice does not identify the challenged presbytery action, the grounds, or any reason for withdrawal. The practical effect was that the matter ended without any merits ruling or relief. It illustrates that a bare withdrawal entry supports only a status synopsis, not an inference about the merits. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__stub_1997-01.html) |
| [1997-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-02.html) | Nickoley v. Rocky Mountain | Remanded | Rocky Mountain Presbytery cited Pastor Bruce Nickoley for contumacy during his trial, after he allegedly refused to tell his congregation to stop picketing, and immediately deposed him without a hearing. On appeal, the SJC sustained the appeal, holding the Presbytery misapplied BCO provisions on confession, citation, refusal to testify, and deposition; Nickoley neither confessed nor refused to appear. Although presbyteries have general authority to maintain order, serious charges require due process. The SJC remanded, recommending either a new process beginning with BCO §32-3 or revocation of the deposition and reinstatement. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-02.html) |
| [1997-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-03.html) | Nickoley v. Rocky Mountain | Administratively out of order; Remanded | Bruce Nickoley complained against Rocky Mountain Presbytery over its action dissolving the relationship with Evergreen Church. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order under SJC Manual 10.1. The same matter was already the subject of an appeal granted to Evergreen Church and docketed for Presbytery's January 22–24, 1997 meeting, and BCO 43-1 provides that no complaint is allowable in a judicial case in which an appeal is taken. No merits ruling was reached. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-03.html) |
| [1997-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-04.html) | Nancy A. Conrad et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Not sustained | After a Session corrected an earlier unauthorized removal from its rolls, then formally voted to remove the same members, the members challenged Presbytery's denial of their complaint, arguing that the new removal defied the prior decision. The SJC upheld Presbytery's action. It concluded that the record showed no unconstitutional procedure or BCO violation and that it could consider only facts properly in the record, not material from earlier cases offered in oral argument. The ruling left the later membership removal undisturbed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-04.html) |
| [1997-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-05.html) | Mt. Carmel Session v. New Jersey Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained; Denied | Mt. Carmel Session challenged New Jersey Presbytery's creation-days resolution, arguing that the Westminster Standards require six consecutive twenty-four-hour days. The SJC majority concluded that Presbytery could resolve the doctrinal question under BCO 11-4 and that prior Assembly actions permitted latitude on the length of the creation days. The General Assembly rejected the minority report, adopted the majority report, and denied the complaint. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-05.html) |
| [1997-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-06.html) | Fitzsimmons v. Evangel Presbytery | Remanded | After a church member and deacon was excommunicated by his session, he appealed to Evangel Presbytery. Presbytery found the appeal in order and appointed a commission, but then rescinded that action and never adjudicated the appeal. The SJC held Presbytery erred by failing to notify the appellant of the appeal hearing and by failing to adjudicate an appeal properly before it. It remanded under BCO 42-9 for proper adjudication and made no ruling on the remaining session-related merits issues. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-06.html) |
| [1997-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-07.html) | Steve Farris v. Central Florida Presbytery | Judicially out of order | The Standing Judicial Commission held Steve Farris's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery judicially out of order because Farris was not a member of a PCA church and therefore lacked standing before the Commission. The Commission reached no merits issue and granted no relief; the only stated ground was the complainant's lack of standing. The case illustrates a threshold standing bar for SJC complainants, but the sparse record does not identify the underlying presbytery action complained of. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-07.html) |
| [1997-08](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-08.html) | Bridie v. Central Florida | Judicially out of order | Whether a non-PCA church member may bring a complaint against a presbytery? The full Standing Judicial Commission held no, finding Theresa Bridie's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery judicially out of order because she was not a member of a PCA church and therefore lacked standing. No merits issue was reached, and the sparse record does not identify the challenged presbytery action. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-08.html) |
| [1997-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-09.html) | Robert M. Shive v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Reversed; Remanded | A church member appealed convictions and excommunication arising from vulgar statements to two patients, challenging the lack of pretrial reconciliation, recusals, the prosecutor’s participation in deliberations, and Presbytery procedure. The SJC left guilt intact and denied a new trial, though it held that a prosecutor may not deliberate as a judge. It reversed excommunication because the record did not show impenitence or contumacy, which could not be inferred from exercising the right to remain silent. It remanded only to impose indefinite suspension from the Sacraments and conditions pending satisfactory evidence of repentance. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-09.html) |

His companion Case 97-12, also against Pacific Presbytery, was withdrawn at the same time. No separate merits opinion was published, so the record supplies only the disposition and no reasons, facts, or relief. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__stub_1997-10.html) |

The SJC answered both issues no and did not sustain the complaint, leaving Presbytery's action undisturbed. It reasoned that approval was conditional under CCP rules, the moderator expressed Presbytery's intention, Presbytery did not surrender jurisdiction, and BCO 39-3 required deference; it found no appearance of prejudice. Vote 11-7, with dissents urging remand and challenging sessional control over committee eligibility. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga26_1998__1997-16.html) |

Susquehanna Valley Presbytery | Denied | A member challenged Presbytery’s approval of a congregational motion supplementing an assistant-pastor fund, alleging that Session had ceded its budget authority. The SJC denied both issues. The motion addressed a special circumstance, not approval of the budget, and left the salary figure to the elders and deacons; Session had already approved the budget and retained control of church funds. | [1998-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga27_1999__1998-01.html) | Snapp v. James River Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | The complaint challenged James River Presbytery's approval of an ordination examination in which the candidate called the Genesis creation days God's anthropomorphic work days, not necessarily twenty-four-hour days. The complainant argued that view conflicted with WCF I.9. The SJC denied the complaint and answered 'No' to whether the Presbytery erred; the examination stood. It held the Presbytery had authority and discretion, no General Assembly had declared anthropomorphic days contrary to the Standards, and an advisory-committee study left the SJC unwilling to decide creation-day length. A six-member dissent sought an exception and study-committee referral. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga27_1999__1998-01.html) |
| [1998-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga27_1999__1998-02.html) | St. Paul Session, et al. v. Central Florida Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | The St. Paul Session and other Central Florida presbyters complained that Presbytery wrongly sustained a commission report denying the Session complaint and declining to find a strong presumption of guilt against Pastor John Hutchinson. The SJC denied the complaint on both issues. It held CFP permissibly directed a BCO 31-2 investigation and chose its own procedures; procedural irregularities and possible bias did not show BCO 39-3 clear error, though the panel criticized CFP’s handling. A lone dissent would remand, alleging the commission ignored the substance of 41 of 45 specifications. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga27_1999__1998-02.html) |

James River Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | At issue was whether James River Presbytery erred by instructing TE Andrew Conrad not to teach or preach his views that the Genesis days were not necessarily six twenty-four-hour days, after JRP treated the views as an exception. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving JRP's instruction in effect. It deferred under BCO 39-3, finding no significant procedural or constitutional error and no clear error of discretion; the parties had stipulated that instruction as the sole issue. The eight dissenters would have found JRP exceeded its discretion. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga27_1999__1998-05.html) |

## 28th General Assembly (2000)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1998-08](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1998-08.html) | Smith v. Southwest Presbytery | Sustained; Reversed | Smith appealed discipline for divisiveness, gossip and slander, broken membership vows, and contumacy arising largely from complaints and letters during church conflict. The SJC sustained her appeal, reversed guilt on all four charges, and annulled suspension from the sacraments. The documentary record proved none of the allegations; filing complaints was not itself divisiveness, and the trial improperly lacked a witness, shifted proof to Smith, showed prejudice, and unfairly rejected her written defense. The SJC declined remand because the evidence was insufficient. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1998-08.html) |
| [1998-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1998-09.html) | Baer v. Illiana Presbytery | Denied | An appeal from a Presbytery judgment and indefinite suspension of a pastor turned on whether he violated the Ninth Commandment and ordination/installation vows by telling the congregation the Session had 'demanded' his resignation for six weeks. The SJC denied the appeal, holding the Session as a whole had not formally demanded resignation; individual elders' earlier opinions did not excuse the overstatement, which harmed the Session's good name. It also found no due-process irregularity or prejudice warranting reversal, deferring to the lower court under BCO 39-3, leaving indefinite suspension in place. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1998-09.html) |
| [1998-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1998-10.html) | Curtis v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Remanded | Eastern Carolina Presbytery referred to the SJC both TE Byron Curtis's complaint against Presbytery's order barring him from teaching his exceptions and TE Jeff Black's already-sustained complaint on the same subject. Without reaching the merits, the SJC remanded to the Presbytery for adjudication at the next stated meeting, directing that Curtis's complaint be heard. It reasoned that judicial complaints in process cannot be referred for mere advice and that, despite uncertainty about what the Presbytery sought, the lower court should hear the case first. Five SJC members dissented; the merits remained open. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1998-10.html) |
| [1999-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1999-01.html) | Western Carolina v. Tennessee Valley  ·  *dissent* | Administratively out of order | Three presbyteries asked the General Assembly under BCO 34-1 to assume original jurisdiction over a minister alleged to have allowed women to preach from a church pulpit. The SJC held the requests administratively out of order and did not reach the allegation’s merits. Worship was the Session’s responsibility, so the minister could not be held liable for actions assigned to it; moreover, Tennessee Valley Presbytery had acted on the allegations, defeating BCO 34-1’s refusal-to-act prerequisite. No further proceedings were ordered. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1999-01.html) |
| [1999-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1999-02.html) | Tan v. South Texas Presbytery | Administratively out of order; Dismissed | Tan's complaint challenged South Texas Presbytery's action at its July 30–31, 1999 meeting. The SJC declared the complaint administratively out of order because it was untimely under BCO 43-3: although dated and faxed August 28, it was not mailed until September 4 and was received September 7—beyond 30 days. SJC Manual 19.10 requires receipt in the Stated Clerk's office and disallows fax filing. The merits were not reached. Twenty-two members concurred; one was recused and one absent. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1999-02.html) |
| [1999-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1999-04.html) | Ed Fitzsimmons v. Evangel Presbytery | Administratively out of order | The SJC refused to hear Ed Fitzsimmons's appeal from Evangel Presbytery because his appeal was not filed with the General Assembly's Stated Clerk within the 30-day deadline of BCO 42-2. The appeal was declared administratively out of order, and no merits question was decided. The sparse record shows a straightforward application of the filing deadline; it does not disclose the underlying presbytery action or any merits view. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1999-04.html) |

| [1999-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__1999-05.html) | Rountree v. Covenant | Partially sustained; Denied | After a minister remained on his presbytery's rolls without call and outside its bounds for more than seven years, the presbytery completed involuntary divestiture without censure. He appealed. The SJC denied the appeal and sustained the divestiture, reasoning that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 allowed the presbytery to follow that procedure once the constitutional three-year limit had long passed and no call to a particular ministry was available. The action therefore left the divestiture without censure in force. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__1999-05.html) |
| [1999-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__1999-06.html) | Robert M. Shive v. Central Carolina Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained | A member challenged Presbytery’s affirmance of his excommunication, contending that SJC Case 97-9 had reversed his four guilty verdicts and precluded increased censure. The SJC did not sustain either issue. Case 97-9 had reversed only the original censure, leaving guilt intact. Because the offender bore the burden of showing repentance, and Session’s contrary factual determination received great deference absent clear error, the later excommunication remained in effect. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__1999-06.html) |
| [1999-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__1999-07.html) | Jeffrey M. Black v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained | Black challenged Presbytery’s handling of his complaint and its ruling that a licentiate’s non-24-hour creation-day view was not an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC denied remand because Presbytery had effectively adjudicated the complaint; the separate objection to proceeding without Black was not first filed below and was administratively out of order. It upheld Presbytery’s ruling that not every non-Calendar-Day view constitutes an exception. Because the record did not identify the licentiate’s precise view, the decision did not determine its acceptability or whether it could be taught. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__1999-07.html) |

Northeast Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Administratively out of order | A prosecutor's complaint relating to Northeast Presbytery's judicial case was held administratively out of order by the SJC. The SJC adopted two grounds: BCO 43-1 bars a complaint about a matter subject to an appeal in another case, and the complaint sought retrial of an accused on charges of which he had been acquitted, relief the SJC could not grant. Although the related appeal was later withdrawn and the withdrawal approved, the SJC still applied BCO 43-1. A concurrence disputed that first ground and urged BCO clarification of appellate review of acquittals. No merits ruling was made. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__2000-02.html) |

## 30th General Assembly (2002)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2000-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2000-09.html) | Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Annulled | After Korean Capital Presbytery appointed a commission to suspend the functions of Korean Presbyterian Church Washington’s elected Session and replace them without prior congregational consent, TE Sung Keon Kim complained. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery violated Preliminary Principle Six and BCO 16-2, misread BCO 13-9, and impermissibly sought to act for the lower court. Relying on Chappell, it annulled the commission’s subsequent actions as the Session. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2000-09.html) |
| [2001-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-01.html) | Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Reversed | The SJC addressed whether a presbytery and its administrative/judicial commission could suspend a local session and assume original jurisdiction over charges against a ruling elder. It answered no: original jurisdiction belonged to the session, and a presbytery cannot "act for" a lower court by replacing congregationally elected elders. Preliminary Principle Six, BCO 16-2, and BCO 31-1/33-1 controlled; the commission's interpretation of BCO 13-9 conflicted with those principles. The Presbytery's and Commission's actions, including the censure approved by Presbytery, were reversed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-01.html) |
| [2001-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-02.html) | Sang Roo Ryoo v. Korean Capital | Sustained; Remanded | Korean Capital Presbytery's commission tried and suspended a Korean church assistant pastor for heresy and schism after he failed to answer two summonses, and Presbytery upheld the suspension. On appeal, the SJC sustained the procedural challenge because no indictment with witnesses had been served and the record lacked any minutes or hearing for the default judgment, contrary to BCO 32-3. The SJC remanded for a new trial but expressly declined to rule on the citations, default procedure, or merits. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-02.html) |
| [2001-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-03.html) | Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | A minister suspended for five years after a default judgment of heresy and schism appealed to the SJC. The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, holding the judicial commission did not follow BCO 32 and 34: no indictment was served, and the record lacked minutes or evidence of a hearing. It remanded to Korean Capital Presbytery for a new trial. The SJC expressly did not reach the merits, the adequacy of the citations, or whether default judgment is proper. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-03.html) |
| [2001-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-04.html) | Moon K. Ham v. Korean Capital | Sustained; Reversed | A ruling elder appealed Korean Capital Presbytery’s three-year suspension of him from the sacraments. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery’s and its Judicial Commission’s actions because original jurisdiction over a communicant member belonged to his local Session. The ruling rests on the identity of the proper court, not the merits of the charges, and orders no remand or further relief. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-04.html) |
| [2001-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__stub_2001-05.html) | RE Moon K. Ham et al. v. Korean Capital Presbytery | Withdrawn | The SJC’s 2002 report records the complaint of Moon K. Ham and others against Korean Capital Presbytery as withdrawn. The withdrawal notice gives no reason for the withdrawal and reports no decision on the underlying dispute. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__stub_2001-05.html) |
| [2001-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-07.html) | Andy Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Annulled | A complaint challenged Presbytery’s suspension of a church Session and installation of a commission to perform Session functions without prior congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled all subsequent commission actions as the Session insofar as the commission was improperly constituted. Presbytery could not suspend elected officers and replace them without prior consent; later recognition could not cure the defect. The SJC also rejected Presbytery’s objection that a related appeal barred the complaint because the cases presented fundamentally different issues. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-07.html) |
| [2001-08](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-08.html) | TE Andy Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* |  |  | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-08.html) |
| [2001-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-09.html) | Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery | Sustained; Reversed | On appeal from an excommunication, the SJC held that Korean Capital Presbytery and its special judicial commission were not the proper court of original jurisdiction to adjudicate charges against a communicant member. Because original jurisdiction belonged to the local session, the Presbytery/commission proceedings against the member were unconstitutional and reversed. The ruling turned only on jurisdiction; it did not decide the truth of the schism and contumacy charges. The excommunication therefore could not stand on that record. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-09.html) |
| [2001-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-10.html) | Charles C. Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery (Appeal) | Sustained; Reversed | A communicant member appealed Presbytery’s findings of guilt and censure of excommunication. The SJC reversed Presbytery’s and its Special Judicial Commission’s actions because original jurisdiction over judicial proceedings against a local church’s communicant member belonged to that church’s Session. The decision was jurisdictional: it neither resolved the underlying charges nor directed a remand or acquittal. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-10.html) |
| [2001-11](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-11.html) | Byung Han Yoo v. Korean Northwest Presbytery | Out of order (type not stated); Dismissed | A ruling elder's complaint against Korean Northwest Presbytery was found out of order because it was untimely under BCO 43-2. The action complained of was taken October 10, 2000, but the complaint was filed March 12, 2001, well outside the 30-day filing period, so the SJC reached no merits question. The case illustrates that a complaint failing BCO 43-2 timeliness is dismissed without adjudication of the underlying presbytery action. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-11.html) |
| [2001-12](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-12.html) | Peter Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery | Sustained; Reversed | The SJC sustained Deacon Peter Lee’s appeal from Korean Capital Presbytery’s censure and reversed the Presbytery and its special judicial commission for adjudicating charges that belonged to the local Session. Lee, a communicant member, had been suspended from the sacraments for five years after the commission found contumacy and a false statement; Presbytery approved. The SJC held that original jurisdiction over a member’s judicial action or censure rests with the Session, not Presbytery or its commission. The reversal was jurisdictional and did not decide the underlying charges. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-12.html) |
| [2001-13](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-13.html) | Samuel Hong v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Reversed | Deacon Samuel Hong appealed after Korean Capital Presbytery's special judicial commission convicted him of contumacy and making a false statement and imposed a two-year suspension from the sacraments. The SJC sustained the appeal, holding that original jurisdiction over charges against a communicant member belongs to the local Session, not Presbytery or its commission, and reversed the Presbytery/commission actions. The SJC did not decide the underlying charges; the reversal was jurisdictional, not an acquittal. One recorded dissent gave no reasons. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-13.html) |
| [2001-14](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-14.html) | Moon K. Ham v. Korean Capital Presbytery | Sustained; Reversed | Ruling Elder Moon K. Ham appealed to the SJC after Korean Capital Presbytery approved a Special Judicial Commission's guilty findings for contumacy, church division/destruction, and a false statement, imposing indefinite suspension from the sacraments (called excommunication in the appeal). The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed Presbytery's and the Commission's actions. Because Ham was a church member, the Session, not Presbytery or its commission, was the proper court of original jurisdiction. The ruling did not remand, acquit, or address the merits. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-14.html) |
| [2001-15](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-15.html) | In Mo Chung v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Reversed | The SJC decided whether a presbytery and its special judicial commission could assume original jurisdiction over disciplinary charges against a church member. It sustained the appeal and reversed: the court of original jurisdiction for communicant members is the local church session. Because the appellant was a member of Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington, the presbytery and its commission acted contrary to constitutional standards when they adjudicated the charges and imposed excommunication. The ruling rested on jurisdiction, not the merits; no remand was ordered. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-15.html) |
| [2001-16](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-16.html) | Joo Bok Suh v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Reversed | In this SJC appeal, RE Joo Bok Suh challenged Korean Capital Presbytery's excommunication after its special judicial commission, rather than his local session, received and adjudicated charges that he had committed contumacy and made a false statement in a civil-court filing. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery/commission action because the court of original jurisdiction over a communicant member is the local session. The reversal was jurisdictional; the SJC did not rule on the truth of the charges, so it was not an acquittal. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-16.html) |
| [2001-17](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-17.html) | Choon Soon Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Reversed | Korean Capital Presbytery approved a three-year suspension from the sacraments after its special judicial commission found RE Choon Soon Lee guilty of contumacy and making a false statement on a civil-court document. On appeal, the SJC sustained and reversed. Because Lee was a communicant member, the Session—not Presbytery or its commission—was the court of original jurisdiction; the commission's adjudication therefore violated constitutional standards. The SJC did not decide the underlying charges, and one commissioner dissented. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-17.html) |
| [2001-18](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-18.html) | Sang Soo Ryoo v. Korean Capital Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | The SJC sustained an assistant pastor’s appeal from a three-year suspension from the sacraments after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission found him guilty of participating in the call of an allegedly unconstitutional presbytery meeting. The decisive defect was procedural: no indictment was served, no prosecutor was clearly appointed, and no trial minutes appeared in the record; service of an indictment with a witness list was critical. The case was remanded for a new trial, and the SJC expressly did not reach the merits or citation adequacy. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-18.html) |
| [2001-19](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-19.html) | Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | On appeal from a minister’s deposition in a conflicted Korean Capital Presbytery church, the SJC asked whether the commission followed BCO procedures in instituting and conducting judicial process. It sustained the appeal, holding that no indictment appears to have been served and the record lacked minutes showing a trial, contrary to BCO 32-3’s writing, indictment, and service requirements. The SJC remanded to Presbytery for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34. It expressly did not rule on the adequacy of the citations or the merits. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-19.html) |

North Florida Presbytery | Not sustained; Affirmed | After TE Anthony Dallison confessed spousal abuse and received an indefinite suspension, North Florida Presbytery later found him impenitent and deposed him and suspended him from the sacraments. Dallison complained that increasing the censure required fresh charges and trial. The SJC disagreed: his BCO 38-1 confession waived trial rights as to the original charge; the offender then had to satisfy the court of repentance, and the presbytery could investigate and impose higher censure under BCO 37-3, 37-4, 37-8, and 34-4b. ## 31st General Assembly (2003)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2001-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-06.html) | Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained | The SJC sustained a complaint by two ruling elders against Korean Eastern Presbytery over a disputed congregational meeting (three commissioners dissented). The session was deadlocked and had not called a requested meeting; KEP's administrative commission called and supervised the February 18, 2001 meeting, and KEP approved that action. The SJC reversed both lower-court actions, holding that BCO 25-2 places responsibility on the session and that the presbytery's proper course was to adjudicate a complaint under BCO 43, not act for the session. It declined to rule on the meeting's legal effect. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-06.html) |
| [2001-30](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-30.html) | Third Presbyterian Church v. Evangel Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Judicially out of order | Third Presbyterian Church asked the SJC to review Evangel Presbytery's denial of its complaint against a Presbytery commission's binding arbitration award of $57,000 to Covenant Classical School. The SJC ruled the complaint not judicially in order, not denied on the merits: PCA courts may not serve as civil arbitrators, and neither Presbytery nor the SJC may review legally binding arbitration judgments. Church courts may act only as ecclesiastical arbitrators, whose decisions lack civil effect and are reviewable under BCO 43. The complaint's five grounds were not reached. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-30.html) |
| [2001-31](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-31.html) | Deacon Neil Jeansonne v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Denied; Remanded | After Deacon Neil Jeansonne was convicted by his Session of causing dissension and strife, Eastern Carolina Presbytery reversed, then reinstated the conviction; the SJC asked whether his General Assembly appeal was properly before it. It was not. Because Case 2001-33 held ECP erred in hearing RE Williams's complaint, ECP's April 21, 2001 reversal and removal of censures stand. The case is remanded to the Session, which may retry using the prior indictment or not pursue the matter. BCO 43-1 barred the complaint once appeal was taken. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-31.html) |
| [2001-32](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-32.html) | Christ Covenant Church Session v. Central Carolina Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Judicially out of order | Christ Covenant Church Session complained under BCO 43 that Central Carolina Presbytery wrongly annulled the session trial commission's judgment and found due-process error concerning H. The SJC did not reach the merits. It held the case not judicially in order because H's complaint to the Session was untimely: it exceeded the thirty-day requirement of BCO 43-2 and came more than eighty days after the oral verdict. The ruling thus turned on a procedural gate, making no merits ruling on Presbytery's annulment or its due-process rationale. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-32.html) |
| [2001-33](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-33.html) | W.W. Marshall Jr. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Sustained | A minister challenged Presbytery’s decision to sustain a complaint that rescinded its earlier appellate reversal of a deacon’s conviction and censures. The SJC sustained the minister’s complaint because BCO 43-1 bars a complaint in a judicial case once an appeal has been taken, whether the appeal is past, current, or pending. It reversed Presbytery’s July judgment, restored the April judgment, and remanded to the Session, which could retry the charges using the prior indictment or decline to pursue them. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-33.html) |
| [2002-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-01.html) | Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Affirmed; Reversed | In a dispute arising from a Korean Eastern Presbytery congregational election, two ruling elders were tried, refused to plead, and were suspended from sacraments and office; KEP denied their appeal, then increased the censures to deposition and excommunication for contumacy. The SJC affirmed KEP's denial and the guilt findings, but reversed the increased censures. An appellate court may not increase a censure under BCO 42-9; the trial court retains discretion to remove or increase an indefinite suspension, though the appellate court may recommend a lesser censure. The original suspension remained. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-01.html) |
| [2002-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__stub_2002-04.html) | Judicial Reference from Evangel Presbytery for Adjudication | Denied | Evangel Presbytery asked the SJC to accept and adjudicate a judicial reference. The SJC did not accede to the request. The published report gives no reason for declining the reference and no judgment on the underlying matter. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__stub_2002-04.html) |
| [2002-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-06.html) | Wright v. Northern California Presbytery | Judicially out of order; Withdrawn | The SJC docket reports that Randall Wright’s appeal against Northern California Presbytery “was found out of order and withdrawn.” No merits opinion followed. The sparse record does not disclose the challenged lower-court action, the grounds, or any relief; it establishes only procedural termination of the appeal. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-06.html) |
| [2002-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-07.html) | Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery | Judicially out of order | The SJC found Nichols and Couch’s complaint against James River Presbytery out of order. The docket report does not identify the challenged Presbytery action, the grounds for the ruling, or an administrative or judicial subtype. No merits opinion followed under this docket number. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-07.html) |
| [2002-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-10.html) | Carolyn Goerig v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained | A church member challenged Pacific Northwest Presbytery's denial of her complaint that Faith Presbyterian Church (Tacoma) Session had banned her from worship and sought to erase her membership retroactively under BCO 38-4. The SJC sustained the complaint. Because she never joined Covenant PCA, BCO 46-3 left her membership under Faith's Session; the Session's proposed retroactive erasure did not comply with BCO 38-4's pastoral-oversight steps. The Presbytery therefore erred and should have remanded the matter to the Session. No separate merits relief beyond that remand directive appears. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-10.html) |
| [2002-11](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-11.html) | Brian Abshire v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained; Denied; Remanded | Abshire challenged Presbytery’s commission for its appointment, scope, exhortation, summary disposition of two elders’ complaint, and other actions. The SJC sustained only the challenge to deciding the elders’ complaint without BCO 43 procedures and remanded that complaint. It denied the other issues: the commission could conduct the required investigation, the scope objection was untimely, and its exhortation and report were pastoral rather than formal discipline. A separate sixth issue remained before Presbytery and was not decided. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-11.html) |
| [2002-12](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__stub_2002-12.html) | Warren E. Gardner v. North Georgia Presbytery | Out of order (type not stated) | TE Warren E. Gardner's complaint against North Georgia Presbytery was found out of order. The supplied record contains no separate merits opinion, issue-level ruling, or adopted reasoning; it only cross-references 31-35, II, p. 93. The practical effect is that the complaint did not proceed to a merits adjudication. The case is useful mainly as a sparse-record example: the disposition is recorded, but the basis for the out-of-order finding is not disclosed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__stub_2002-12.html) |
| [2002-13](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__stub_2002-13.html) | Lachman v. Philadelphia | Out of order (type not stated) | Philadelphia Presbytery was the respondent in a complaint by RE David C. Lachman et al., but the record does not identify the challenged action. The General Assembly found the complaint out of order. No separate merits opinion was published, and the stub supplies no issue-level rulings, reasons, or relief beyond the out-of-order disposition and a cross-reference to 31-35, II, p. 93. It therefore supports only a status note, not a merits synopsis. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__stub_2002-13.html) |

The same minute entry also records that a request that the SJC accept and act upon the judicial reference in Case 2002-04 was not acceded to. It therefore documents only a procedural status, not the complaint's substance or the basis for the ruling. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__stub_2002-15.html) |
