## 32nd General Assembly (2004)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2002-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-05.html) | Plowman v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | A church session suspended a member from the Lord's Table and found her guilty of contumacy. The chairman of Presbytery's Judicial Business Committee advised her that her appeal was out of order; Presbytery later ruled her complaint untimely. The SJC sustained her complaint: she had submitted to regular trial, making her appeal in order under BCO 42-2, and her complaint was timely after Presbytery's advice caused the appeal to be renamed. It remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the appeal. Filing the appeal suspended the Lord's Table censure pending final adjudication; the SJC questioned the contumacy ruling. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-05.html) |
| [2002-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-09.html) | Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery | Denied | The SJC denied TE Stuart H. Merriam's appeal from Tennessee Valley Presbytery's April 20, 2002 conviction on three ordination-vow specifications and its indefinite suspension. It rejected procedural challenges—that the earlier called meeting was improperly convened and that TVP was prejudiced by prior cases—and found no clear error, applying BCO 39-3(2)'s deference to lower-court factual findings. The SJC sustained TVP's judgment; prior SJC Cases 95-10 and 96-7 had only indirect bearing and did not require retrial. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-09.html) |
| [2002-14](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-14.html) | Lachman v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Denied | A ruling elder convicted by his Session of fifth-, sixth-, and ninth-commandment violations challenged the conviction because the prosecution presented no live witness and relied on his own letters. The SJC denied the appeal and upheld Presbytery's affirmance, holding that the documents, Lachman's acknowledgments of writing them, and defense witnesses supplied sufficient proof; the Session also followed Matthew 18 with patience. A concurrence urged change-of-venue procedures for small-Session bias cases, but noted Lachman never requested a reference or challenged the court before trial. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-14.html) |
| [2002-16](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-16.html) | Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church v. Louisiana Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained | The SJC sustained a session's timely complaint that Louisiana Presbytery barred one of its members from the Lord's Table after assuming original jurisdiction. Under BCO 33-1, a presbytery may assume jurisdiction only when the session 'refuses to act'; because the session had investigated and found no strong presumption of guilt, it acted, so LAP never acquired jurisdiction. The censure was therefore a nullity, and the member remained under his session. The SJC also held the jurisdictional assumption reviewable despite no timely complaint against it. Three commissioners dissented. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-16.html) |
| [2002-17](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-17.html) | Sung K. Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Judicially out of order | TE Sung K. Kim appealed his deposition by Korean Capital Presbytery, but the SJC declared the appeal judicially out of order. Because Kim had not submitted to a regular trial, he was not entitled to appeal under BCO 42-2; the Presbytery had instead found him guilty of contumacy and deposed him from office under BCO 34-4. The ruling disposes of the appeal without reaching its merits and leaves the deposition in force. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-17.html) |
| [2002-18](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-18.html) | Mark Herzor and Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Judicially out of order | Case 2002-18 is a complaint (the heading also says "Reference") identified in the adopted motion as TE Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery. The SJC found it judicially out of order because it was filed against actions of a judicial commission, not completed Presbytery actions (BCO 15-3, 43-1). The full SJC approved that action on October 16, 2003. No merits ruling or later dismissal is stated; the Manual only outlines a possible dismissal route. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-18.html) |
| [2003-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2003-01.html) | Mark Chavalas v. Northern Illinois Presbytery | Sustained | Chavalas appealed a Northern Illinois Presbytery judgment, but testimony cited by both parties was missing from the record. Because recording-machine failures made the required transcripts unavailable and Presbytery could not cure the defect, the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order, dismissed it under SJC Manual 11.6, and suspended Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7. Chavalas’s later resignation did not abandon the appeal because he had appealed beforehand after a regular trial; no rebuke was issued. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2003-01.html) |
| [2003-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2003-06.html) | Wright v. Eastern Carolina  ·  *dissent* | No final disposition in available record | The SJC found Case 2003-6 judicially out of order because the challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery action was only advice in response to a BCO 41-1 reference from White Oak Session, not a binding or complainable doctrinal decision under BCO 41-3. The underlying dispute—whether elders could hold and teach a broader atonement view—was therefore not reached. The adopted vote was 17 concurring, 1 dissenting, with 1 abstention and 4 absent. The dissent argued Presbytery's 'not allowed' language read as compulsory final disposition. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2003-06.html) |
| [2003-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2003-07.html) | Aureliano Tan v. South Texas Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Administratively out of order | TE Aureliano Tan filed a complaint against South Texas Presbytery with the SJC before the presbytery had heard it. The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order as prematurely filed, so it reached no merits. The adopted vote was 19 concurring, 0 dissenting, with 4 absent; the full SJC approved the ruling on March 4, 2004. The same pages separately contain proposed SJC Manual changes and a dissent, not a ruling in this complaint. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2003-07.html) |

## 33rd General Assembly (2005)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2001-34/2002-02/2002-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2001-34_2002-02_2002-03.html) | Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained | Church members challenged Presbytery’s repeated delay in granting a properly adopted congregational request to dissolve its pastoral relationship and its gift equivalent to three months of the pastor’s compensation. The SJC found seven complaints judicially out of order, sustained the dissolution-delay challenge, and rejected the gift challenge because Presbytery controlled its own civil property. No further relief was ordered. A concurrence would permit delay based on objective, justifiable findings, but concluded that Presbytery’s stated grounds were insufficient. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2001-34_2002-02_2002-03.html) |
| [2001-34/2002-02/2002-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2001-34_2002-02_2002-03.html) | Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained | Three complaints arising from Presbytery’s treatment of Session actions toward its pastor were judicially out of order. Complaints 10-01 and the unnumbered complaint were filed directly with the SJC without first being presented to James River Presbytery, contrary to BCO 43-2. Complaint 13-01 challenged an action never taken because the motion was ruled out of order. The SJC did not reach their merits. The combined decision’s pastoral-dissolution and benevolent-gift rulings concerned the other consolidated cases, not Case 2002-02. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2001-34_2002-02_2002-03.html) |
| [2001-34/2002-02/2002-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2001-34_2002-02_2002-03.html) | Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained | Ruling elders challenged James River Presbytery’s delay in honoring West End’s valid congregational vote to dissolve its pastoral relationship and a three-month salary gift to the pastor. The SJC held that Presbytery lacked a constitutional basis to delay the dissolution, but rejected the challenge to its benevolent use of its own civil funds. Complaints 16-01, 18-01, and 19-01 were judicially out of order; the others were in order. No remand or repayment was ordered. A concurrence cautioned that prompt dissolution is not automatic when objective, justifiable findings support refusal. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2001-34_2002-02_2002-03.html) |
| [2003-02/2003-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-02_2003-05.html) | Thornton v. Westminster  ·  *dissent* | Remanded | Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s investigation of TE Frank Smith’s secret recording and its refusal to institute process. The SJC remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation because Presbytery had not timely obtained the other participant’s testimony or examined relevant legal and confessional questions. It rejected claims concerning alleged lying and threats, partiality, and an unbiblical recording policy. The invitation of an outside voluntary prosecutor was moot because he declined; only a separate concurrence found the invitation improper. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-02_2003-05.html) |
| [2003-02/2003-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-02_2003-05.html) | Thornton v. Westminster  ·  *dissent* | Remanded | Thornton challenged Presbytery’s investigation and refusal to institute process against Smith over secretly recording Roberts, alleged lying and threats, partiality, and its taping policy. The SJC sustained only the challenge to the secret-taping investigation: the committee failed to interview Roberts before reporting and examine the legal and confessional implications of transcription and destruction. It remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation. The other claims lacked sufficient proof; the voluntary-prosecutor issue was moot because Roberts declined. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-02_2003-05.html) |
| [2003-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-03.html) | Paul W. Lee v. Korean Southwest | Sustained | A minister appealed three convictions and suspension that would automatically become indefinite absent repentance. The SJC sustained the appeal: unauthorized committee citations and admonition without process could not support guilt, and multiple trial violations were fatally prejudicial. It set aside the judgment, dismissed the citation and admonition charges, and revoked both censures. The inappropriate-language charge was not adjudicated on its merits; Presbytery could retry it on remand or dismiss it. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-03.html) |
| [2003-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-04.html) | Dr. and Mrs. Frank Chin v. Covenant Presbytery | Not sustained | The Chins complained to the SJC after Covenant Presbytery denied their complaint against Covenant Presbyterian Church Session's refusal to examine their young children for admission to the Lord's Supper. The SJC did not sustain the complaint. Its adopted reasoning held that BCO 57-2 leaves the time for examining young persons to the Session's prudence and imposes no mandate to examine every child put forward; if the Session decides the time has come, careful examination is required. The dissent read BCO 57-1 as requiring examination of covenant children seeking admission. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-04.html) |
| [2004-01/2004-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-01_2004-10.html) | Westminster Presbyterian Church v. Westminster Presbytery | Withdrawn | Westminster Presbyterian Church’s complaint against Westminster Presbytery was withdrawn. The SJC docket report gives no reason for the withdrawal, identifies no merits determination, and records no further relief or proceedings. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-01_2004-10.html) |
| [2004-01/2004-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-01_2004-10.html) | Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery | Withdrawn | The appeal of TE Stuart Merriam against Tennessee Valley Presbytery was withdrawn. The report does not identify the challenged judgment, explain the withdrawal, or provide a merits opinion. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-01_2004-10.html) |
| [2004-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-02.html) | Nancy J. Plowman v. Philadelphia Presbytery | Sustained | A member suspended from the Lord's Table appealed after Presbytery let the Session resume her trial and failed to lift all suspensions. The SJC sustained the appeal, finding the Session's premature censure, truncated trial, and prosecutor-judge conflict manifested prejudice and made a fair trial impossible. It set aside all judgments and censures, treated the November 13, 2003 communion letter as non-censuring advice, and did not remand. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-02.html) |
| [2004-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-03.html) | Tim J. Harris v. Heritage Presbytery | Not sustained | A church member challenged Heritage Presbytery's ruling that the BCO neither expressly nor implicitly requires a congregation to approve changes in a pastor's call, and that it does not require the session to publicize budget details. The SJC held the BCO silent on both points: once the original call and terms are approved, later changes are budgetary and belong to the session under BCO 12-5b; publicizing the budget is prudent but not mandated. The complaint was not sustained; seven commissioners dissented, arguing congregational approval follows by good and necessary consequence. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-03.html) |
| [2004-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-04.html) | Jerguson v. Western Carolina | Judicially out of order | The SJC held Jerguson’s appeal judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 because Western Carolina Presbytery was rehearing the case. The matter therefore was not ready for higher-court review. The decision did not reach the merits or dismiss the underlying Presbytery proceedings. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-04.html) |
| [2004-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-05.html) | Blevins v. Westminster | Sustained | SJC sustained TE Philip Blevins's complaint against Westminster Presbytery, holding the Blevins/Seufert complaint was timely despite the commission's February 3, 2004 untimeliness ruling. The wife's April 2003 letter was essentially a BCO 35-13 request to review new evidence, and the Session's May 2003 denial was a new complaintable decision. The SJC did not decide the wife's divorce grounds or the Session's merits; it remanded for Presbytery to rehear the Session and Warhurst complaints with the Blevins/Seufert merits considered. A concurrence added that no full new trial is required. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-05.html) |
| [2004-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-06.html) | Aureliano Tan Jr. v. Houston Metro Presbytery | Judicially out of order | Tan attempted to appeal without first submitting to a regular trial. The SJC found the appeal judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 and therefore did not reach its merits. Although the source header labels the disposition “dismissed,” the adopted judgment expressly classifies it as judicially out of order. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-06.html) |
| [2004-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-07.html) | Session of First Presbyterian Augusta v. Savannah River Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained | A presbytery annulled a session's actions after the session added to a petition-called congregational meeting a recommendation that the congregation invoke BCO 24-6 against eleven elders. The SJC sustained the session's complaint: BCO 25-2 permits a session to add agenda items, and BCO 24-6 does not require a member-initiated motion; the congregation's own 503–229 vote began the process. It reinstated the session's actions, declared remaining relief moot, and noted one recorded dissent; no dissent text appears. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-07.html) |
| [2004-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-09.html) | Scott Robar v. Central Carolina Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Judicially out of order; Dismissed | The SJC found RE Scott Robar's appeal from Central Carolina Presbytery judicially out of order and dismissed it because he filed his notice of appeal only with Presbytery's stated clerk, not also with the General Assembly's stated clerk as BCO 42-4 requires. No merits review of his conviction occurred. Four commissioners dissented, arguing that the presbytery clerk's admittedly incorrect advice, Robar's reliance, and Presbytery's request to treat the appeal as timely should excuse the filing defect under the Plowman precedent and equity or estoppel principles. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-09.html) |
| [2004-11](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__stub_2004-11.html) | Scott v. Northern California Presbytery | Moot | A teaching elder's appeal against Northern California Presbytery was found moot. The published entry on page 71 identifies neither the challenged ruling nor the reason for mootness, and no separate merits opinion was published. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__stub_2004-11.html) |
| [2004-12](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__stub_2004-12.html) | Hunt v. Western Carolina | Out of order (type not stated) | Mr. M. E. Hunt sought review of an unidentified action by Western Carolina Presbytery. The Assembly record reports that his complaint was found out of order, without identifying an administrative or judicial subtype. It provides no reason, merits determination, relief, or further proceedings. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__stub_2004-12.html) |

## 34th General Assembly (2006)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2004-08](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2004-08.html) | Thornton v. Westminster Presbytery | Sustained | Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s refusal to place Memorial PCA Session’s call in his hands and its simultaneous initiation of administrative divestiture without censure. The SJC sustained both issues, reversed the divestiture decision, and remanded with directions to approve and deliver the call and set an installation date. A valid call supplied the congregational approbation whose absence BCO 34-10’s administrative remedy requires; Presbytery also could not rely on undisclosed concerns while avoiding required judicial process. The ruling found clear error, not an absence of all presbyterial review authority. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2004-08.html) |
| [2004-13](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__stub_2004-13.html) | Zaepfel v. Central Carolina Presbytery | Abandoned | Complaint 2004-13, TE Wayne Zaepfel v. Central Carolina Presbytery, was abandoned at the 34th General Assembly (2006). The available record gives no merits analysis, adopted reasons, or relief beyond the statement that this case was abandoned; it serves only as a disposition notice, not as authority on the underlying complaint. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__stub_2004-13.html) |
| [2005-01](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2005-01.html) | Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained; Affirmed | An appeal challenged a presbytery's conviction of a minister for divisive behavior and its indefinite suspension from office and the sacraments. The SJC affirmed: the charge was lawful because publicly publishing disagreement with the session after it acted violated his ordination vows to subjection and peace/unity, even though “divisive” is not a constitutional term; the censure was not unjust absent repentance; procedural errors did not require reversal or remand. A dissent argued the charge failed BCO 29-1’s Scripture-proof requirement. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2005-01.html) |
| [2005-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__stub_2005-02.html) | Andrino v. | [2005-08](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2005-08.html) | Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Not sustained | A minister appealed convictions for contumacy and threatening elders with civil litigation, plus deposition and excommunication. The SJC sustained contumacy as failure to remain subject to the brethren under the ordination vow, not BCO 32-6-type contumacy. It sustained deposition but found excommunication excessive given the conflict and replaced it with indefinite suspension from the sacraments. It did not sustain the threat conviction because the attorney’s letter was absent from the record. A dissent disputed the contumacy ruling. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2005-08.html) |
| [2005-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2005-09.html) | Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery (Complaint)  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Moot | A minister challenged Presbytery’s denial of his complaints concerning a congregational petition and an Administrative Commission’s actions. The SJC sustained both issues: the petition should first have gone to the Session, and Presbytery and its Commission committed additional constitutional errors. Those errors did not excuse his refusal to obey Presbytery, however. Because he had been deposed in Case 2005-8, further action was moot; the SJC granted no remedy, vacatur, or remand. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2005-09.html) |

## 35th General Assembly (2007)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2006-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__2006-06.html) | Ehrlich v. North Georgia | Denied | Members challenged Presbytery’s denial of their complaint against a Session instruction not to circulate an open letter repeating allegations against their pastor. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving the instruction in force. It held that liberty of conscience does not eliminate members’ obligation to obey lawful church injunctions. Here the members had sought the Session’s advice, Presbytery had found no strong presumption of chargeable offenses, and renewed circulation would disturb the church’s peace; under those circumstances, the Session acted within its authority. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__2006-06.html) |
| [2006-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__2006-07.html) | Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Out of order (type not stated) | Chastain appealed Heritage Presbytery’s 2006 excommunication and deposition. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order because Chastain had renounced PCA jurisdiction on May 8, 2006. Consequently, Presbytery’s later proceedings were moot and SJC 2005-1 remained in effect. The SJC did not reach the merits. A concurrence questioned the discipline process after renunciation; a dissent argued the majority lacked constitutional authority to recognize unilateral withdrawal and thereby undercut discipline. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__2006-07.html) |
| [2007-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__stub_2007-05.html) | Mitchell v. Evangel | Withdrawn | Dr. George W. Mitchell’s appeal against Evangel Presbytery was withdrawn. The 35th General Assembly record reports no merits decision, reason for the withdrawal, or ruling on the unidentified underlying dispute. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__stub_2007-05.html) |
| [2007-05](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__stub_2007-05.html) | Mitchell v. Evangel | Withdrawn | Dr. George W. Mitchell’s appeal against Evangel Presbytery was withdrawn. The 35th General Assembly record reports no merits decision, reason for the withdrawal, or ruling on the unidentified underlying dispute. | [disposition](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__stub_2007-05.html) |
| 2007-04 | Stephen P. Engel v. Evangel Presbytery | sustained |  | _decided at 36th GA_ · [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-04.html) |
| 2007-06 | Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery | not_sustained |  | _decided at 36th GA_ · [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html) |

## 36th General Assembly (2008)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2006-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2006-02.html) | Memorial of Central Carolina v. Louisiana | Sustained | In a BCO 40-5 memorial, Central Carolina Presbytery alleged that Louisiana Presbytery had exonerated TE J. Steven Wilkins despite his published views on election, the church, perseverance, assurance, and baptism allegedly contradicting the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the memorial’s gravity and found Presbytery failed to show due diligence, ordering a recorded examination, formal responses, and report. Presbytery later met the procedural directives, but the SJC relied on Case 2007-8’s substantive finding, cited Presbytery under BCO 40-5, and appointed a prosecutor for Case 2007-14. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2006-02.html) |
| [2007-01/2007-06/2007-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html) | Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery | Partially sustained | Lee challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s actions affecting his interim pastoral relationship, alleging that its October 3, 2006 meeting lacked a quorum. The SJC held the complaint moot and declared every action taken at that meeting null and void—not merely those concerning his church. The meeting opened with only two ruling elders when three were required, and the minutes did not establish when a quorum was later achieved; its presence therefore could not be presumed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html) |
| [2007-01/2007-06/2007-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html) | Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery | Denied; Affirmed | Lee challenged irregular Presbytery meetings, classification of his interim pastorate as stated supply, expiration of his term, and appointment of a Judicial Commission. Meeting-related concerns were moot or resolved by nullification; the SJC otherwise denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery. No pastoral call had been approved or installation conducted, and BCO 22-6 limited the stated-supply relationship to one year absent renewal. The ruling approved only the Commission’s appointment, not its later actions, which remained subject to pending complaints. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html) |
| [2007-01/2007-06/2007-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html) | S. Han v. Korean Eastern Presbytery | Denied; Affirmed | RE Han challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s treatment of TE Lee as stated supply rather than pastor, its clarification of its earlier action, and its appointment of a Pulpit Commission. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery: Lee lacked an approved pastoral call or installation, “interim pastor” meant stated supply under BCO 22, and his unrenewed one-year term had expired. BCO 15-2 permitted the commission’s appointment to process stated-supply requests. The ruling did not approve or disapprove the commission’s later actions. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html) |
| [2007-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-02.html) | Malone v. Metro NY | Partially sustained; Vacated | Malone challenged Presbytery’s approval of a commission’s judgment and indefinite suspension imposed without process. The SJC sustained the complaint in part and vacated the judgment and censure: the commission had authority only to investigate, and Malone’s general acknowledgments neither confessed specific charges nor showed intent to waive process under BCO 38-1. Presbytery could begin anew under proper procedures. The SJC rejected Malone’s claim that suggested steps evidencing repentance improperly bound him, treating them as noncompulsory pastoral advice. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-02.html) |
| [2007-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__stub_2007-03.html) | Segallis v. Central Florida | Out of order (type not stated) | The 36th Assembly (2008), on the SJC docket, recorded the complaint of Greg Segallis et al. against Central Florida Presbytery as out of order (36-31, p. 75). No separate merits opinion or reason for the out-of-order disposition appears in the supplied record; the stub supports only that disposition. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__stub_2007-03.html) |
| [2007-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-04.html) | Stephen P. Engel v. Evangel Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal to decide his guilt or innocence and its failure to return charges after his Session suspended him from the sacraments without trial or confession. The SJC sustained the complaint on the remand issue: rescission of the censure did not dispose of pending charges, so Presbytery had to rehear the complaint and require the Session either to institute proper process or dismiss them. It declined to determine guilt without a trial record and rejected the claim that the censure’s prescribed form willfully took the Lord’s name in vain. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-04.html) |
| [2007-08](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-08.html) | Jones v. Louisiana | Sustained | Louisiana Presbytery’s refusal to institute process after examining Steve Wilkins’s Federal Vision teachings was challenged for applying the wrong constitutional standard and overlooking a strong presumption that some views were out of conformity with the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s denial. A “difference” need not expressly contradict the Standards; Presbytery must independently investigate and classify it rather than accept the member’s assurance or shift the burden to objectors. The ruling did not adjudicate Wilkins’s guilt; the Central Carolina memorial remained before the SJC. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-08.html) |
| [2007-12](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-12.html) | Grady v. Southwest Florida  ·  *dissent* | Sustained | A minister complained that Presbytery placed a shepherding committee report containing findings of his alleged “sins and errors” in its minutes and directed that it be read to his congregation. The SJC sustained the complaint and ordered the report expunged. Although a committee may form and record an opinion without judicial process, Presbytery's endorsement and public dissemination effectively admonished the minister on unsubstantiated and unproven opinions without due process. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-12.html) |
| [2007-14](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-14.html) | PCA v. Louisiana Presbytery (Trial)  ·  *dissent* | Guilty; Dismissed | In this BCO 40-5 proceeding over Louisiana Presbytery’s investigation of TE Stephen Wilkins, the SJC dismissed Specification 1 because it could not find that the cited procedures were constitutionally required or that guilt was proved. The dismissal did not erase concerns about undocumented doctrinal findings; those failures were covered by Specification 2. On Presbytery’s guilty plea to that specification, the SJC imposed a public admonition for failing to find a strong presumption of doctrinal guilt and pursue trial. Wilkins’s and his church’s withdrawal made practical amends unavailable. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-14.html) |
| [2007-15](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__stub_2007-15.html) | Sang C. Choi v. Korean Central | Out of order (type not stated) | TE Sang Chul Choi’s complaint against Korean Central Presbytery was found out of order. The sparse published record does not identify the challenged presbytery action, specify an administrative or judicial subtype, explain the ruling, or resolve the merits. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__stub_2007-15.html) |
| [2007-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__stub_2007-03.html) | Segallis v. Central Florida | Out of order (type not stated) | The 36th Assembly (2008), on the SJC docket, recorded the complaint of Greg Segallis et al. against Central Florida Presbytery as out of order (36-31, p. 75). No separate merits opinion or reason for the out-of-order disposition appears in the supplied record; the stub supports only that disposition. | [disposition](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__stub_2007-03.html) |

Korean Central | Out of order (type not stated) | TE Sang Chul Choi’s complaint against Korean Central Presbytery was found out of order. The sparse published record does not identify the challenged presbytery action, specify an administrative or judicial subtype, explain the ruling, or resolve the merits. | [disposition](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__stub_2007-15.html) |

## 37th General Assembly (2009)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2007-09/2007-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-09_2007-10.html) | Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery (2007-09 & 2007-10) | Sustained; Annulled | Lee challenged Presbytery’s authorization of its Pulpit Commission to act for HKPC’s Session. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s decision and the Commission’s resulting actions, and directed return of expended church funds if the congregation requested. Neither the Session nor congregation had requested or consented to that authority. The ruling distinguished the Commission’s valid appointment to receive stated-supply requests from its impermissible empowerment to function as the Session or pulpit committee. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-09_2007-10.html) |
| [2007-09/2007-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-09_2007-10.html) | Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery (2007-09 & 2007-10) | Sustained; Annulled | Lee challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s ratification and filing of a New Jersey lawsuit through a commission acting for the local church, seeking civil adjudication of who was the rightful pastor and who could act as the church’s session. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s decision in whole. PCA courts have moral and spiritual, not civil coercive, authority and cannot sue to enforce ecclesiastical decisions. The ruling does not prohibit litigation over purely civil matters and did not condemn the commission’s original appointment. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-09_2007-10.html) |
| [2007-11](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-11.html) | Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern | Sustained; Reversed | After Korean Eastern Presbytery tried, convicted, deposed, and excommunicated TE Eliot Lee, the SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the disposition and excommunication. The decisive reason was procedural: the record did not show timely service of the indictment/citations or the required 14-day trial notice, violating BCO 32-3, 32-7, and 32-10. Under BCO 42-9, the SJC rendered the decision it thought should have been made, finding no strong presumption of guilt under BCO 31-2 justified formal process; it added pastoral counsel, expressly not censure. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-11.html) |
| [2007-13](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-13.html) | David Kniseley et al. v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | On complaint from TE David Kniseley and others, the SJC reviewed Rocky Mountain Presbytery's refusal to forbid a mission church from giving an unordained female staff member the title 'Minister of Church Life.' The SJC denied the complaint. It held the BCO uses 'minister' synonymously with pastor and teaching elder, but is silent on general use for non-ordained staff; a lower court may exercise discretion subject to BCO 40-2(3)'s WESP review. The decision addressed only the constitutional issue, not the title's wisdom or propriety; four commissioners dissented. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-13.html) |
| [2007-16](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-16.html) | Grady v. Southwest Florida  ·  *dissent* | Affirmed; Reversed; Vacated; Remanded | A minister appealed convictions and indefinite suspension arising from conflict over Presbytery's direction that he resign. The SJC upheld all three convictions, finding two procedural errors nonprejudicial and rejecting the other preserved challenges. But Presbytery could not treat its authority to dissolve a pastoral relationship as authority to compel resignation on pain of discipline. The SJC therefore vacated the censure and dissolution of the call and remanded for reconsideration of censure; Grady's separate administrative suspension remained effective. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-16.html) |
| [2008-01/2008-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-01_2008-10.html) | Session of Crossroads Community Church v. Philadelphia Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied; Affirmed | Two consolidated complaints challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s licensing and ordination of a candidate who believed Scripture could permit women to hold the deacon’s office but promised to follow the BCO and not ordain women. The SJC denied both complaints and affirmed Presbytery. It distinguished subscription to doctrinal standards from approval of BCO practices, applied a three-part inquiry, and deferred to Presbytery on the candidate’s credible vow. Because complainants identified no violated doctrinal standard, no error was shown. The ruling reaffirmed that the BCO bars ordaining women as deacons. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-01_2008-10.html) |
| [2008-01/2008-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-01_2008-10.html) | Mark Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied; Affirmed | The complaint challenged Presbytery’s approval of a candidate who believed women could hold the diaconal office but promised to follow the BCO, which permits only men to be ordained as deacons. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed approval of his ordination examination. It held that a BCO difference is evaluated through compliance, doctrinal, and ordination-vow inquiries; the record supported compliance and a credible vow, while complainants had not identified violated doctrinal standards. Absent contrary evidence, Presbytery’s judgment received deference. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-01_2008-10.html) |
| [2008-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__stub_2008-02.html) | Hofland v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery | Withdrawn | The 37th General Assembly recorded this complaint by TE Fred Hofland and others against Eastern Carolina Presbytery as withdrawn. No merits opinion was published, and the record does not identify the challenged action, explain the withdrawal, or grant relief. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__stub_2008-02.html) |

The sparse published record does not identify the challenged presbytery action, classify the ruling as administratively or judicially out of order, or explain its basis. No merits decision was published. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__stub_2008-03.html) |

| [2008-09](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-09.html) | Session of Red Mountain Presbyterian Church v. Evangel Presbytery | Sustained; Reversed | Red Mountain Session challenged Presbytery’s ruling that it had inadequately addressed a member’s demand to declare his wife’s divorce unbiblical, and Presbytery’s resulting declaration and Matthew 18 instruction. The SJC sustained all four issues and reversed Presbytery. It held Session’s context-sensitive ruling disclosed no clear error, use of BCO 31-2 was reasonable, Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by allowing its commission to revise a report after floor discussion, and Presbytery judged the wife without due process. The SJC expressly did not decide whether biblical divorce grounds existed. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-09.html) |

## 38th General Assembly (2010)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2008-11](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-11.html) | Broadwater et al. v. Chesapeake Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained; Vacated | Presbytery empowered a commission both to assume original jurisdiction over matters involving church members and to receive a Session's reference concerning a membership transfer. The SJC vacated the original-jurisdiction mandate because Presbytery had neither found that the Session refused to act nor required the commission to make that finding before proceeding. The authority to receive the reference remained intact; requests from other Sessions alone did not satisfy BCO 33-1. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-11.html) |
| [2008-13](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-13.html) | Meyerhoff v. Chesapeake Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Moot | Meyerhoff challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s called meeting to receive, discuss, and entertain questions about an original-jurisdiction commission’s initial report. Without deciding whether those actions were procedurally erroneous, the SJC held the complaint moot in view of its judgment in Case 2008-11. It directed Presbytery to note the mootness ruling in the minutes of the August 16, 2008 meeting. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-13.html) |
| [2008-14](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-14.html) | White v. Siouxlands Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Remanded | A minister complained that his presbytery wrongly refused to order a BCO 31-2 investigation into another minister’s Covenant of Works/Federal Vision views. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded for that investigation, holding that BCO 31-2 requires investigation of credible, injurious reports about Christian character. The presbytery erred by applying the higher evidentiary standard for conviction after process; reports sufficient to trigger investigation need not establish guilt or a strong presumption of guilt, and hearsay or conflicting testimony can require investigation rather than justify refusal. A concurrence agreed in result; the dissent found no clear error in the presbytery’s exercise of discretion. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-14.html) |
| [2008-15/2008-16/2008-17/2008-18/2009-01/2009-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) | Morton Smith v. Western Carolina | Partially sustained | The complaint challenged Presbytery’s commissions and its response to a canceled congregational meeting. The SJC upheld the Inman Commission because a Session may reference limited duties without congregational consent. It sustained the challenges to Presbytery’s consideration of the August 7 meeting and appointment of the Sealy Commission because the Session majority had validly canceled the meeting. Linton’s and Pellom’s calls therefore remained undissolved and Neville was uncalled, absent later congregational action. The SJC also upheld Presbytery’s criticism of the cancellation as unwise and its refusal to issue a BCO 40-5 citation. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) |
| [2008-15/2008-16/2008-17/2008-18/2009-01/2009-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) | Hutchinson & Bulkeley v. Western Carolina | Denied; Affirmed | Ministers challenged Presbytery’s handling of RE Payne’s confession as a BCO 38-1 case without process, asking the SJC to declare it incomplete and require prosecution of additional alleged sins. The SJC did not sustain the complaint. It held that a complaint cannot bypass the BCO 33-1 and 34-1 procedures by seeking relief akin to original jurisdiction. Further allegations could be filed as formal charges with Payne’s Session, which could investigate, prosecute, or reference the matter to a higher court. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) |
| [2008-15/2008-16/2008-17/2008-18/2009-01/2009-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) | Hutchinson & Bulkeley v. Western Carolina | Partially sustained | Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s decision to suspend RE Neill Payne indefinitely from office but not from the Sacraments. The SJC did not sustain the complaint: BCO 30-3 expressly permits suspension from office without sacramental suspension, and no provision requires both censures together. Because the appropriate censure involved discretion and judgment, the SJC deferred absent clear error. Authority to remove or increase Payne’s censure had returned to his Session. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) |
| [2008-15/2008-16/2008-17/2008-18/2009-01/2009-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) | Hutchinson & Bulkeley v. Western Carolina | Partially sustained | Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s refusal to condemn RE Neill Payne’s views in a circulated “Africa e-mail.” The SJC did not sustain the complaint. It held that a presbytery may not condemn a church officer’s allegedly erroneous opinions without due process and that four sentences, an approving newspaper reference, and the Commission’s summary did not present Payne’s views fully enough for responsible adjudication. The SJC rejected race or intelligence as the primary determinant of a nation’s fate, while allowing the e-mail to be used as evidence in formal charges. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) |
| [2008-15/2008-16/2008-17/2008-18/2009-01/2009-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) | Morton H. Smith v. Western Carolina Presbytery | Referred | Smith challenged Presbytery’s ruling that his complaint was filed too late. The SJC gave no independent yes-or-no answer on timeliness, instead answering by reference to Case 2008-15. That decision held the August 7 congregational meeting illegitimate and voided resulting Presbytery actions and related complaints. The record does not identify which particular ruling in 2008-15 controlled Smith’s complaint. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) |
| [2008-15/2008-16/2008-17/2008-18/2009-01/2009-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) | Leissing v. Western Carolina | Partially sustained | Leissing challenged Presbytery's November 7 action dissolving the calls of REs Linton and Pellom. By reference to Case 2008-15, the SJC sustained the complaint: the Session had canceled the August 7 congregational meeting, so it generated no valid dissolution request and Presbytery erred in appointing the Sealy Commission. The Commission proceedings, the complaint against its decision, and Presbytery's resulting dissolution action were voided; absent subsequent congregational action, the elders' calls remained undissolved. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html) |
| [2009-02](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-02.html) | Morton Smith v. Western Carolina | Partially sustained; Annulled; Remanded | Smith challenged Presbytery’s reversal of a finding that an elder’s race-and-IQ views did not create a strong presumption of guilt and its immediate judgment against those views. The SJC upheld the reversal as a discretionary determination, without addressing its merits, but annulled the declaration against the views because a strong-presumption finding required judicial process. On remand, Presbytery was to commence process against the elder or rescind that finding and drop the matter. The ruling did not restrict Presbytery’s ability to adopt general position statements outside an investigation. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-02.html) |
| [2009-05/2009-08/2009-09/2009-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html) | Payne v. Western Carolina Presbytery | Not sustained; Denied; Affirmed | Four complainants challenged Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt, citing delayed action and failure to interview accusers. The SJC denied the complaints: BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but grants great discretion and prescribes neither interviews nor a timetable, and the record showed no clear constitutional error overcoming deference to Presbytery. Lyons and Woodward also lacked standing because they were not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. No renewed investigation or process was ordered. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html) |
| [2009-05/2009-08/2009-09/2009-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html) | Linton v. Western Carolina Presbytery | Denied; Affirmed | An elder challenged Presbytery’s failure to interview accusers, alleged investigative delay, and resulting finding of no strong presumption of a pastor’s guilt. The SJC denied the complaint. BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but prescribes no timeline or interview procedure, giving courts substantial discretion before formal process begins. The ordinary stated-meeting sequence used here disclosed no clear constitutional error. The SJC therefore deferred to Presbytery’s superior proximity to the facts and upheld its finding. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html) |
| [2009-05/2009-08/2009-09/2009-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html) | Lyons v. Western Carolina Presbytery | Partially sustained; Denied | Lyons challenged Presbytery’s investigation of accusations against a teaching elder, alleging failure to interview accusers, undue delay, and an erroneous finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC denied the complaint and additionally held that Lyons lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. The consolidated opinion explained that BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but prescribes neither interviews nor a timeline; finding no constitutional or clear factual error, it deferred to Presbytery’s judgment. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html) |
| [2009-05/2009-08/2009-09/2009-10](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html) | Woodward v. Western Carolina Presbytery | Denied | Robert Woodward challenged Presbytery’s acceptance of a finding that accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley did not raise a strong presumption of guilt, alleging investigators never heard his evidence. The SJC denied the complaint, specifically holding that Woodward lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. It also held that BCO 31-2 prescribes no interview requirement or fixed timeline and found no clear constitutional error warranting departure from ordinary deference to Presbytery. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html) |
| [2009-06](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-06.html) | Bordwine v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Sustained; Reversed; Remanded | Pacific Northwest Presbytery adopted a report finding TE Peter Leithart's views not out of accord with the fundamentals of the system of doctrine. The SJC sustained a complaint, holding PNW erred because, without formal judicial process, it lacked authority to declare either that the views were out of accord or that they were not. The record still suggested a strong presumption of guilt. The SJC refused complainants' affirmative declaration and remanded with directions for pastoral counsel under BCO 31-7 and possible BCO 31-2 compliance. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-06.html) |
| [2009-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-07.html) | Urish v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery | Denied; Affirmed | The SJC denied James Urish and others' complaint against Rocky Mountain Presbytery for sustaining Dan Breed's ordination exam. Breed had said women could teach Scripture to mixed adults in settings like Sunday school under session oversight, but not preach, hold elder office, or teach outside session authority. Because the Westminster Standards and BCO did not expressly resolve that view, the SJC found no clear error under BCO 39 and affirmed Presbytery's denial. A concurrence criticized Breed's exegesis of 1 Tim. 2:12 but stressed the SJC was not endorsing it. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-07.html) |
| [2009-11](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-11.html) | Larry Edison et al. v. Southwest Florida Presbytery | Partially sustained | Ministers complained that Southwest Florida Presbytery improperly reexamined Bryan Gregory and reversed his examination, membership, and call after previously receiving him. The SJC upheld Presbytery’s authority to hear and sustain the earlier complaint but sustained the present complaint on the remedial actions. Sustaining a complaint did not itself undo prior acts; once Presbytery had treated Gregory as a member, his membership rights could be removed only through disciplinary due process. The SJC annulled the reexamination and March 24 actions and directed Presbytery to consider appropriate remedies. Gregory’s theology was not before it. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-11.html) |
| [2009-13](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-13.html) | Johnson v. Southwest Florida | Administratively out of order | An unspecified complaint against Southwest Florida Presbytery was found administratively out of order. The published record does not identify the challenged action or explain the administrative defect, and no separate merits opinion, relief, or further proceedings are reported. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-13.html) |
| [2009-14](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-14.html) | Session of Ellisville Presbyterian v. Grace | Withdrawn | The Ellisville PC Session’s complaint against Grace Presbytery was withdrawn, and the 38th Assembly recorded that disposition (38-31, p. 129). The stub publishes no merits opinion and states no reason for the withdrawal; the case therefore supplies no ruling on the complaint’s underlying dispute. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-14.html) |
| [2009-15](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-15.html) | Robinson v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery | Judicially out of order | The Assembly recorded TE Mark Robinson et al.'s complaint against Metro New York as judicially out of order. The published stub does not identify the challenged action, explain the procedural defect, decide the merits, or specify relief. The header's contrary description of the disposition as administratively out of order appears erroneous. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-15.html) |

It does not identify the challenged action, type of proceeding, administrative defect, or any merits ruling or relief; the case therefore supports only that procedural status, not a substantive holding. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-16.html) |

The published notice does not identify the challenged action or the reason for that ruling, and reports no merits determination, additional relief, or further proceedings for this docket. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-17.html) |

The published record is only a stub: it gives no merits opinion, no allegations, and no rationale for the administrative ruling, and it states no further proceedings. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-27.html) |

## 39th General Assembly (2011)

| Case | Parties / Title | Disposition | Summary | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2009-12/2009-21](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-12_2009-21.html) | Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | Presbytery refused to hear Armes’s complaint against his excommunication, initially reasoning that excommunication deprived him of standing and later ruling the complaint untimely. Presbytery conceded its error on the standing ground, and all parties stipulated to remand for a hearing. The SJC confirmed that stipulation, sustained the complaint, and remanded the case without deciding the validity of the excommunication itself. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-12_2009-21.html) |
| [2009-12/2009-21](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-12_2009-21.html) | Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Partially sustained; Remanded | Armes challenged Presbytery's refusal to hear his second complaint about Session's trespass notice and threat of arrest, which Presbytery treated as duplicating his pending excommunication complaint. The SJC sustained the complaint because the trespass action occurred later and was distinct, although the matters could be heard together. It remanded for Presbytery or a commission to hear the complaint under BCO 43-8. The SJC did not decide whether Session could issue such a notice; review remained subject to timely filing and standing. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-12_2009-21.html) |
| [2009-22](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-22.html) | McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery | Denied | The SJC denied a censured husband's complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery's approval of a judicial commission report, which had upheld his session's refusal to receive his charges against his wife after she filed for civil divorce. Applying BCO 39-3.2–3.3, the SJC deferred to the lower courts' factual and discretionary findings absent clear error. It found no clear procedural error, upheld the conclusion that the wife did not sin by seeking civil protection, and invoked BCO 31-8's caution about accusations from one under censure. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-22.html) |
| [2009-23](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-23.html) | Koerkenmeier v. Illiana Presbytery | Sustained | Illiana Presbytery appointed a commission with broad power 'to deal with matters' at Center Grove Presbyterian Church after a pastor requested inquiry into alleged evils. The SJC sustained the complaint but held the error harmless: the broad charge could take original jurisdiction from the session contrary to BCO 11-3 & 4 and 33-1, while a limited investigative committee under BCO 13-9(f) and 31-2 would have been proper. Because the commission never exercised that power and the session endorsed its findings, no remedy, including invalidation of the adopted report, was ordered. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-23.html) |
| [2009-24](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-24.html) | Phelps v. Pacific Presbytery | Denied | Phelps complained that Pacific Presbytery erred by finding no constitutional irregularities in the New Life Burbank Session's ordination of Lee Irons as a ruling elder, despite PP's earlier refusal to receive Irons as a teaching-elder candidate. The SJC denied the complaint. Under BCO 39-3.3, the Court owed great deference to the lower court's discretionary fitness judgment; the single office of elder does not require identical eligibility processes, and the NLB Session had jurisdiction after Irons renounced OPC jurisdiction. PP's action stood; the SJC declined to decide the NAPARC issue. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-24.html) |
| [2009-25/2009-26](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-25_2009-26.html) | Brown v. Northern California Presbytery | Sustained; Annulled | Brown challenged Presbytery’s abstract approval of six views concerning diaconal practice. The SJC sustained the consolidated complaints and annulled Presbytery’s action because a church court cannot issue a binding decree apart from properly exercising jurisdiction over specific persons. Constitutional conformity must instead be determined through authorized examination or judicial processes. The judgment deliberately left unresolved whether any of the six views themselves were faithful to the Constitution; the detailed view-by-view analysis appeared only in a concurring opinion. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-25_2009-26.html) |
| [2009-25/2009-26](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-25_2009-26.html) | Session of Grace Presbyterian Church v. Northern California Presbytery | sustained | Joined with Case 2009-25; the Session of Grace Presbyterian Church complained that views 3, 4, 5, and 6 in Northern California Presbytery's resolution on diaconal practice violated the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint on the same grounds as 2009-25, annulling the abstract resolution while declining to rule on the… | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-25_2009-26.html) |
| [2009-28](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-28.html) | Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery | Sustained; Remanded | Nashville Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of reports against TE George Grant was inadequately documented and internally inconsistent, and the evidence before Presbytery raised a strong presumption of guilt, the SJC held. It sustained the complaint, ruling that pastoral reconciliation does not displace the duty to institute judicial process, and remanded for further proceedings; it did not adjudicate Grant guilty. A concurrence agreed only in remanding to supplement the record under BCO 42-5 & 7. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-28.html) |
| [2010-03](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2010-03.html) | McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery | Judicially out of order; Dismissed | An appellant under suspension from the sacraments challenged the presbytery's judicial commission process and censure. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order—not decided on the merits—because he had not submitted to a regular trial, as BCO 42-2 requires. Treated as a complaint, it was also out of order: it had not first been presented to the presbytery, and the 30-day period had expired. The SJC further barred complaints about later court actions while he remained under censure, except as to the highest censure. The censure stood. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2010-03.html) |
| [2010-04](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2010-04.html) | Sartorious et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery  ·  *dissent* | Denied | A complaint challenged Siouxlands Presbytery's investigation of allegations that TE Joshua Moon held heterodox Federal Vision views and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC held that Presbytery had investigated diligently under BCO 31-2 and, deferring under BCO 39-3 to its credibility judgment, found no clear error. It declined to decide whether the overture should have been treated as charges because that issue was not raised below, while leaving future charges possible. A concurrence favored charges; the dissent would have found error and remanded. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2010-04.html) |
| [2010-07](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__stub_2010-07.html) | Sang C. Choi v. The Standing Judicial Commission, in the 39th General Assembly (2011), found 2010-07 administratively out of order, listing it among seven cases (2009-29, 2009-30, 2009-31, 2010-06, 2010-07, 2010-17, 2010-25) disposed of on that ground. No separate merits opinion was published, and the adopted record gives no reason for the ruling or any underlying facts. | [full text](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__stub_2010-07.html) |

WCP dismissed the charges, then ruled Lyons's complaint administratively out of order for lack of standing. The SJC answered that the dismissal was not erroneous—Presbytery had discretion under BCO 31-8, 34-2, and 32-20, and the record showed no clear error—but that WCP erred on standing because Lyons's filing brought him under its jurisdiction.
